data_stores: acp_contract.search_demand — one row per (keyword, market), no tenant column. Columns used: search_volume, people_also_ask, serp_domains, retrieved_on. Written by segment research (volumes, ideas, SERP) and the question top-up (market 'US-PAA2'). Read by atom_ranking demand/questions, T2 tenant_market_seo, S1 prefetch cache-first, T9/T8 place_paa tier.
acp_contract.segment_research_log — one row per (canonical_place, market) with researched_at. Freshness is FRESH_FOR = 182 days. Written only when every purchase for the place succeeded.

silver_aa_internal.seo_context — one row per tour, written by S1 only (process_seo / s1_seo_prefetch) for the S1 tenant's single market (US for AA). Fields: keyword_ideas from keywords_for_keywords seeded by tour title/activity, top_keywords, PAA and related searches from one SERP on the tour seed. Reused for 180 days. Read by T2 (fallback), T8 signal + T9 keyword snapshot, quarter-plan dfs_relevance, admin SEO pages and DOCX export.
Redis seo:<seed>:<location>[:ideas_v3] — 7-day cache of process_seo results shared across tours with the same seed (handler.py:33-38, 156-160).
acp_contract.atom_ranking — demand_volume per (market, tour, segment), plus questions and total_rank. Recomputed by the recompute job ('score' stage) for all 6 markets. Feeds the Slate.
acp_contract.atom_segment.questions_count / contested — caches. questions_count is filled by precompute_question_landings. contested has no writer found in code.
acp_shared.angle_gate_request.dfs_paa_snapshot — per-request snapshot of the T8 signal (seo_context PAA/related + chain questions). T9 reads the keyword and tour PAA from it.
shared.dfs_call_log (spend ledger), shared.spend_budget (dfs/llm caps per kind), shared.unmapped_market_requests (queue of markets tenants declared but DFS_LOCATION_MAP lacks).
gaps: DUPLICATION BETWEEN THE TWO STORES (one direction only): S1 prefetch reads search_demand first (s1_prefetch.py:310-328, MIN_CACHED_IDEAS=5) and skips its SERP when the cache has PAA (:383). But neither S1 path ever writes search_demand (handler.py:257-277, s1_prefetch.py:261-275). So keywords, volumes and PAA bought per tour by S1 (about 16.65 USD of keywords_for_keywords in October) are invisible to atom_ranking, the Slate, T2's tenant-market lookup and the T9 place tier. Research can then buy volumes again for the same keywords. Research never reads seo_context. Result: the same Google data is bought twice under two shapes. Any purchase should land in search_demand (keyword × market) first; seo_context should become a per-tour view built from it.

RESEARCH DOES NOT REACH THE SLATE: segment_research_job.py:44-80 never enqueues a recompute. Demand reaches atom_ranking.demand_volume only at the next unrelated recompute. Proven 08/11: Blog-eligible Segments went from 4 to 31 after a manual recompute.

SERP BOUGHT PER MARKET THOUGH EVERY CONSUMER IS MARKET-AGNOSTIC: _serp_tool (segment_research.py:380-421) buys one SERP per market where the keyword has volume, with no cache check. But the questions axis pools PAA across all markets (atom_ranking.py:709-718), T9/T8 place_paa reads any market and keeps English only (real_questions.py:11, 90-92, 386-451), T2 PAA only reads the same market, and serp_domains feed nothing (see the contested gap). DE/FR/NL SERPs return mostly non-English PAA that T9 throws away but the questions axis may still count. SERP is about 47% of real spend.

atom_segment.contested has NO writer (grep: only SET NULL in atom_ranking.py:339 / segment_research.py:341). compute_contested is imported but never called (debate.py:37). The Debate contested cut never fires, and the stored serp_domains are dead data. Either wire a writer (free, no DFS) or stop treating domains as a reason to buy SERPs. Not checked against the live DB.

LLM keyword proposals are not persisted: segment_research_batch._propose (:170-211) re-asks Haiku every run, so running markets in separate runs pays the LLM N times and can propose different keywords per market. Fix: store place → keywords (with a prompt version) and reuse it across markets and refreshes. Running all target markets in one job shares the proposal today.

RESEARCH SCOPE BUYS USELESS PLACES: the platform branch reads every atom_segment row (segment_research.py:628-633), orphans included. The scoped branch uses tour_atoms, not v_active_tour_atoms (:610-619). There is no transit/unnamed exclusion, but ranking excludes those places (atom_ranking resolve_exclusions :720-725), so money spent on them never reaches the Slate. The 7,323 in-scope count is inflated by an unmeasured amount.

T2 MARKET LOGIC: it uses singular resolve_buyer_market (s1_prefetch.py:430), so only the tenant's first market counts (UK+AU means UK only), while the Slate uses every declared market. T2 PAA comes only from same-market search_demand rows (cached_ideas :153-168), so a design that buys SERP once (US/en) would leave UK/AU/DE T2 without PAA unless T2 reads PAA from any English market, as T9 does. Fallback is the US admin seo_context row (labelled admin_us_fallback).

T2 SCORE RISK WHEN DATA ARRIVES: validate's DFS_INTENT_UNDERUSED (graph.py:1215-1236) subtracts 1.0 from a T2 draft (never a v2 draft) whenever keywords are given and none appears in seo_title/meta. Under the S271 interim, T2 status is validate-only. Filling search_demand for tenant markets therefore switches on a penalty for tours that currently get no keywords. T2 has no source-coverage filter on keywords (S1 v2 has relevant_keywords: ≤3, covered by the source, s1_writer_v2.py:109-127), so the writer can be pushed to force a raw query into the title. Recommend reusing relevant_keywords for T2 before (or together with) the purchase.

T8 relevance/related_keywords, T9 SEO keyword (choose_keyword from snapshot.related_keywords) and quarter-plan dfs_relevance all come from the per-tour US/AA seo_context. None of them uses the tenant market or search_demand. A tour S1 never fetched (or whose row has expired) gives these stages nothing, even when search_demand has rich data for its places.

SLATE BEST-MARKET PICK (slate.py:274-300, :289): the Blog bar reads demand/questions of the market with the lowest total_rank. Because unmeasured demand takes the median rank, a market with no data (DE/FR/NL) can win and hide a real US/UK volume. That causes Blog false negatives. Read MAX demand across the tenant's markets for the bar instead (questions are market-independent anyway).

Unknown tenant markets (CA 2, SG 2, AE 1, HK 1, NZ 1) are dropped silently (resolve_buyer_markets, seed_builder.py:412-445). Only a row in unmapped_market_requests records it. There is no proxy map (CA→US, NZ→AU, SG/HK/AE→UK) and no UI label.

MAX_PLACES_PER_RUN=200 (admin_segment_research.py:44) means about 36 approvals for one US catch-up. estimate_cost (segment_research_batch.py:131-147) overstates real DFS spend about 2× and LLM spend about 5×. Docstrings are stale: '7 days' in segment_research_job.py:5 (actual 182) and 'only path that buys DFS' in admin_segment_research.py:1-14 (S1 also buys).

Unmeasured costs: Jev decide() calls in research (a3_research keyword/idea gates), ranking (a3_demand_belongs) and S1 (a1_seo). Cohere embedding of newly landed PAA at recompute. The off-ledger DFS drop of about 0.7–1.5 USD on 27/10, 28/10 and 01/11. Real shared.spend_budget rows were not read (read-only task).

DESIGN PROPOSAL ('one buyer, one store, every writer reads'). (1) Keyword map: one Haiku proposal per rankable place (persisted place → keywords). Scope = places of active tours via v_active_tour_atoms, minus transit/unnamed/orphan (reuse resolve_exclusions). (2) Tier V, volumes: every mapped keyword × every target market in full 1,000-keyword tasks. Cheap: about 0.09 per 390 places per market. (3) Tier Q, PAA: ONE SERP per place, US location / English, for its best keyword with volume>0 in ANY market (option: volume ≥100). Never per market. Store PAA under the keyword's US row and let T2/T9/A3 read PAA market-agnostically, English only. (4) Tier I, keywords_for_keywords: OFF in pass 1. Later only for Blog-relevant places still at zero volume, and only in full 20-seed tasks. (5) After each run, enqueue one debounced platform recompute (score + route; landing limited to the researched Segments). (6) S1 becomes read-only like T2: seo_context is built free from search_demand (title + atom places, AA market). Buy only if a tour still has fewer than N keywords after research, and route that purchase into search_demand. v2 uses only ≤3 source-covered keywords, so S1 needs little. (7) T2: plural tenant markets (best volume across them), PAA from any English market, keywords filtered with relevant_keywords. T8/T9 relevance and keyword fall back to search_demand by the piece's places when seo_context is missing. (8) Slate Blog bar reads MAX demand across the tenant's markets, and reports no-data vs below-bar. (9) Proxy markets for unsupported countries, labelled in the UI. (10) Cadence: incremental monthly run for new or renamed places after re-atomize (cap ~2–5 USD/month); volumes refreshed every 182 days; PAA every 365 days. Replace the 200-place cap with a USD gate. (11) Wire the contested writer (free) or stop storing domains. (12) Guard test: no v1_*/T2/T7/T8/T9 module imports a DFS client.

COST ESTIMATE, all 6 default markets, measured 08/11 rates (2.565 keywords/place = 395/154; 77.3% of places get a SERP = 119/154; LLM 0.000253 USD/place = 0.039/154; volume task 0.09 per ≤1000 keywords; SERP 0.002). Stale places: US 6,962, UK/AU 7,145, DE/FR/NL 7,243 (in scope 7,323), before the unmeasured exclusion filter, so every figure below is an upper bound for scope. Volumes per market ≈ 18–19 tasks: US 1.62, UK 1.71, AU 1.71, DE 1.71, FR 1.71, NL 1.71, about 10.2 USD for all 6. LLM keyword map, once for all markets: ~1.85 measured (ceiling 0.28 per 200 places = 10.3). New-design SERP, one per place in US/en: ~11.3 (7,323 × 0.773 × 0.002), about half that if gated to volume ≥100 (unmeasured share). TOTAL pass 1, new design, 6 markets ≈ 23.3 USD (~17.7 with the ≥100 SERP gate; ceiling ~35). US+UK+AU only ≈ 18.2; adding DE/FR/NL later costs only ~5.1 (volumes; PAA already bought). Same scope under today's design (SERP per market, ideas on, separate runs per market) ≈ LLM 6×1.85 + volumes 10.2 + SERP up to 6×~11 + ideas ~7.5 (84 tasks, primary market) ≈ 80–95 USD ceiling. Monthly incremental (~300 new places, 6 markets) ≈ 0.54 volume-task floor + 0.46 SERP + 0.08 LLM ≈ 1.1 USD per run; batch monthly, not weekly, because each run pays at least one task per market. S1 saving: a full-catalogue S1 rerun with expired seo_context would buy ~13 USD (batched prefetch) to ~82 USD (per-tour process_seo, 892 × 0.092). Read-only S1 makes that 0. Current seo_context rows (October) expire around April 2027. DFS balance 27.41 USD: 6-market pass 1 fits (~23) but leaves ~4; recommended order is US+UK+AU (~18), measure Blog coverage, then DE/FR/NL volumes (~5), with a top-up decision before any refresh.

Google Ads Keyword Planner API (free with an Ads account), to evaluate only: it gives volumes and keyword ideas (the same source DFS resells for search_volume/keywords_for_keywords) but NO People Also Ask and no SERP domains, so Tier Q still needs DFS. Known constraints, to verify before relying on them: it needs a developer token approved for Basic access plus an OAuth/manager-account setup; accounts with little or no ad spend get bucketed volume ranges instead of exact numbers (a range like 1K–10K still answers the ≥1000 Blog bar, but not the rank-sum demand axis); rate/quota limits and terms-of-use review. At ~10 USD per full 6-market volume pass on DFS, the saving is small for the integration effort; worth revisiting only if volume refreshes become frequent.

name: Approach A: one demand store, one buyer, every writer reads it (place-keyed, tour views derived)
summary:
DataForSEO is bought in one place only: the batched segment-research path. It writes one store, acp_contract.search_demand (keyword x market), plus a new persisted place->keyword map. Every writer only reads that store: S1, T2, T7, T8, T9 and A3 ranking. Tour-level SEO for S1 and T2 is no longer bought per tour. A new demand_profile module builds it for free from the store, using the tour's title places, its active atom places and its activity words. silver_aa_internal.seo_context stays, but only as a materialised AA/US copy of that profile, so the admin pages and the DOCX export keep working.

Purchases come in three tiers. Tier V is volumes: every mapped keyword in all 6 default markets, packed into full 1,000-keyword tasks (cheap, about 1.7 USD per market). Tier Q is questions: one SERP per place, never one per market. It runs in the English market (US/UK/AU) where the place's best keyword has the most searches, and stores PAA, related searches and organic domains in one call. Tier I (keywords_for_keywords) is off in pass 1. It comes back later only for zero-volume places that matter for Blog, and only in full 20-seed tasks.

There is no new queue table. The work list is derived as 'live rankable places minus fresh research log rows', so a re-atomize, rename or dedupe makes new places due automatically. Each A3/place job ends by refreshing a free, pending research plan with a cost estimate. The tech lead approves the plan in admin, or a standing monthly allowance covers it. A successful run enqueues one debounced platform recompute, so the Slate sees the new demand.

Cost at measured rates for all 6 markets: pass 1 about 23.4 USD (21.5 DFS + 1.9 LLM). That falls to about 17.7 USD if the SERP is gated to volume >=100; the ceiling is about 35. Today's design over the same scope costs about 80-97 USD. Steady state is about 3.6 USD/month with 182-day volume and 365-day PAA refresh, or about 1.1 USD/month for new places only. An S1 full-catalogue rerun stops buying DFS (it saves 13-82 USD per rerun).

Recommended run order:
- R0: free dry-run with the new scope filter, to get exact numbers.
- R1: keyword map + US/UK/AU volumes (about 1.9 LLM + 5.0 DFS). This also measures the >=100 share for free.
- R2: one SERP per place (about 5.7-11.3, an exact quote after R1).
- Recompute, then measure Blog coverage.
- R3: DE/FR/NL volumes (about 5.1).
The full pass uses 21.5 of the 27.41 USD DFS balance. A top-up is needed before the first refresh cycle.

per_consumer.stage: Admin segment research (the ONLY DFS buyer)
per_consumer.gets: Scope = places of active platform tours (v_active_tour_atoms) minus transit/unnamed/orphan places (reuse atom_ranking.resolve_exclusions), so money only goes to places that can reach the Slate or a writer. Phases are selectable per run: keyword map, volumes (all chosen markets in full 1,000-keyword tasks), questions (one English SERP per place, skipped when any market row of that keyword has PAA younger than 365 days), and ideas (off by default). Two estimates come before the run: expected cost at measured rates and the ceiling. A USD gate replaces the 200-place cap. Every DFS call carries job_id and reason in shared.dfs_call_log.

cost_6_markets.first_pass_usd: About 23.4 USD all-in: DFS 21.5 + LLM 1.9. Breakdown: volumes 10.17 + SERP 11.32 + LLM keyword map 1.86. With the SERP gated to best volume >=100 it is about 17.7 (DFS 15.8). Ceiling about 35.1 (DFS 24.8). Staged: R1 = keyword map + US/UK/AU volumes = 1.86 LLM + 5.04 DFS. R2 = one English SERP per place = 11.32 (5.66 if gated; the exact quote is free after R1 because the volume distribution is then known). R3 = DE/FR/NL volumes = 5.13. US+UK+AU total = 18.2. The DFS part (21.5) leaves about 5.9 of the 27.41 USD balance. For comparison, today's design over the same scope costs about 80-97 USD: 6 separate LLM proposals 11.1 + volumes 10.2 + SERP per market up to 6×11.3 = 67.9 + ideas 84 tasks = 7.6. An S1 full-catalogue rerun with expired seo_context would also stop costing 13 USD (batched prefetch) to 82 USD (892 × 0.092 per-tour process_seo).
cost_6_markets.monthly_usd: Recommended policy is about 3.6 USD/month (about 44 USD/year): volumes refreshed on a rolling 182 days, PAA on a rolling 365 days, plus about 300 new places/month. The parts: volumes (7,323/6 + 300 = 1,520 places × 2.565 = 3,899 keywords, 4 tasks/market × 6 = 24 tasks) 2.16 + SERP for new places (300 × 0.773 = 232) 0.46 + PAA refresh (5,659/12 = 472 SERP) 0.94 + LLM for new places 0.08. A lean option costs about 1.1 USD/month: new places only (1 task/market = 0.54 floor + 0.46 SERP + 0.08 LLM), with a separately approved full volume refresh every 6 months (about 10.2). Skipping refresh for markets with no live tenant (e.g. DE/FR/NL) halves the volume line. Batch monthly, never weekly: each run pays at least 1 task per market (0.54 USD for 6). A suggested standing cap is dfs/research_monthly = 5 USD.
cost_6_markets.method: Measured rates from the 08/11 run (154 US places): 395 keywords → 2.565 keywords/place; 119 SERP → 77.3% of places get a SERP; LLM 0.039/154 = 0.000253 USD/place. Prices: search_volume 0.09 per task of ≤1,000 keywords per market; serp_advanced 0.002 per keyword per location; keywords_for_keywords 0.09 per ≤20 seeds. Stale places from today's free previews: US 6,962; UK/AU 7,145; DE/FR/NL 7,243; in scope 7,323. Volume tasks per market = ceil(stale × 2.565 / 1000): US 18 (1.62), UK/AU/DE/FR/NL 19 each (1.71), so 113 tasks = 10.17. LLM keyword map is once for all markets, because it is persisted: 7,323 × 0.000253 = 1.86 (ceiling 0.28 per 200 places = 10.25). SERP is one per place, not per market: 7,323 × 0.773 × 0.002 = 11.32; the ceiling with every place having volume in some market is 7,323 × 0.002 = 14.65; the >=100 gate assumes ~50% of places qualify (unmeasured) = 5.66. Today's-design comparison: 6 × 1.86 LLM + 10.17 + 6 × 11.32 SERP + ceil(7,323 × 0.227 / 20) = 84 idea tasks × 0.09. Every figure is an upper bound for scope because the transit/unnamed/orphan exclusion is not yet measured (R0 dry-run gives it free). Not costed: Jev decide() calls (keyword/idea gates, a3_demand_belongs), Cohere embedding of newly landed PAA at recompute, the off-ledger DFS drop of ~0.7-1.5 USD, and whether a full 1,000-keyword task is still billed as one task (the largest seen is 395).

Questions are about the place and mostly portable, but some can be US-centric (visas, flights). Mitigation: choose the location by max volume, and allow a per-market SERP only when a paying tenant asks.

Mitigation: a country×activity keyword set in the map (rides in the last partial volume task, about 0-0.54 USD). DFS balance: the full 6-market pass uses about 21.5 of 27.41 USD. Rolling refresh (about 3.6 USD/month) needs a top-up within about 2 months, or the lean 1.1 USD/month policy.

Recompute load: a platform recompute after each research run re-ranks 6 markets and re-embeds newly landed PAA. Debounce and invalidation-limited landing keep it bounded, but a large pass can still be a long job. Do not run it during an S1 wave (DM-11.4 job-idle rule for deploys/migrations).

freshness: Volumes: per (place, market), fresh for 182 days (FRESH_FOR, unchanged), refreshed on a rolling basis inside the monthly plan (about 1/6 of the catalogue per month), not in one big sweep. PAA, related searches and SERP domains: per keyword, fresh for 365 days (new paa_retrieved_on), refreshed rolling, optionally only for Blog-relevant places. The daily stale-share check per market opens or updates one issue above a threshold.
markets: The 6 defaults (US, UK, AU, DE, FR, NL) all get volumes for every rankable place, because volumes are cheap when packed: about 1.7 USD per market per full pass. Tenant use: the Slate, T2, T8 and the quarter plan read every market a tenant declares (plural), taking max demand across them. name: Approach C: minimum-spend tiered research. Every place gets volumes in every market; questions are bought only where writing will happen; S1 and T2 read the store and never buy
summary:
One buyer (the admin/platform research job) fills one store (acp_contract.search_demand). It buys in three tiers, cheapest first:

1. Tier V: Google volumes for every rankable place × all 6 default markets, packed into full 1,000-keyword tasks (about 1.7 USD per market).
2. Tier Q: one People Also Ask (PAA) SERP, US location, English. It is bought only for places that will really be written about:
   (a) a pre-emptive "Blog shortlist": places whose best keyword clears the per-market Blog demand bar in any market and that hold fewer than 3 fresh English questions;
   (b) an on-demand queue that tenant actions fill for free and a capped platform job drains: a Blog Subject that clears demand but lacks questions, the places on a picked Blog Route, the places of a T2-rewritten tour.
3. Tier I (keywords_for_keywords): OFF.

PAA becomes market-agnostic (English, from any market) for every reader. That covers T2, T9, T8 and the questions axis, so we never buy a SERP per market again.

Every writer reads the store, including S1 and T2:
- S1 stops buying. Its seo_context is built free from search_demand (place keywords ranked by volume, PAA from the place rows). Writer v2 only uses ≤3 keywords covered by the source anyway.
- T2 reads every tenant market (plural, with proxies) and takes PAA from any English market. Its keywords pass through the S1 v2 relevant_keywords filter, so the DFS_INTENT_UNDERUSED penalty cannot hit T2 on raw queries.
- T7 Slate uses a relative Blog demand bar per market. It reports no_data / below_bar / questions_pending.
- T8, T9 and the quarter plan fall back to search_demand by the piece's places when the US/AA seo_context is missing.

Every paid run enqueues a debounced platform recompute, so purchases reach the Slate the same day.

Unsupported tenant countries use labelled proxy markets: CA→US, NZ→AU, SG/HK/AE→UK. A real market is bought only when a paying tenant needs it.

The contested writer gets wired in for free from the US SERP domains.

Cost at the rates measured 08/11, all 6 markets:
- First pass ≈ 17 USD: DFS 15.2 (range 14.0–16.2) + LLM 1.85. Hard ceiling ≈ 26.5.
- Recommended in two approvals: Stage 1 US+UK+AU ≈ 11.5 USD, then Stage 2 DE/FR/NL ≈ 5.5 USD.
- After that: about 0.9–1.8 USD per monthly incremental run, plus a semiannual volume refresh (~10 USD) and a yearly PAA refresh (~5 USD), about 3–4 USD/month amortised.

Comparison:
- Today's design over the same scope: 80–95 USD.
- "One SERP for every place with volume" (design A in the gap list): ~23 USD.
- A full S1 catalogue rerun no longer buys 13–82 USD of DFS.

Pass 1 fits the 27.41 USD DFS balance and leaves about 12 USD. Google Ads Keyword Planner: evaluate only, not in pass 1. It gives no PAA, needs a developer token with Basic access and an OAuth/manager-account setup, low-spend accounts get bucketed volumes, and its terms need review. It would save at most ~10 USD per 6-market volume pass.

cost_6_markets.method:
Inputs: today's live facts. Keywords per place 2.565 (395/154 on 08/11). Share of places with volume > 0: 77.3% (119/154). LLM 0.000253 USD per place (0.039/154). Volume task 0.09 USD per ≤1,000 keywords per market. SERP depth 1: 0.002. SERP depth 2: ~0.00225 (AA-779: 8 calls, 0.018). Stale places: US 6,962; UK and AU 7,145; DE, FR and NL 7,243. Scope 7,323.

(1) Tier V per market = ceil(stale × 2.565 / 1000) × 0.09:
- US: 17,858 keywords → 18 tasks → 1.62.
- UK and AU: 18,327 → 19 → 1.71 each.
- DE, FR and NL: 18,578 → 19 → 1.71 each.
- Sum for 6 markets: 10.17.
- Worst case with all 4 keywords per place: 29 tasks per market → 15.7.

(2) LLM keyword map, once for all markets: 7,323 × 0.000253 = 1.85. Ceiling: 7,323/200 × 0.28 = 10.25.

(3) Tier Q:
- Places with volume: 7,323 × 0.773 = 5,661.
- Shortlist share s (places whose best keyword clears the bar in some market) is UNMEASURED; assumed 25–40%, central 33%. Basis: 178 of 785 US volume keywords reach ≥1000; a top-quartile relative bar gives about 25% per market, and the union over 6 markets is a little higher.
- Shortlist = 1,415–2,264 places (central 1,868).
- Cost = N × 0.002 + 30% depth-2 retries × N × 0.00225 = 3.79–6.06 (central 3.74 + 1.26 = 5.00). The 30% retry share is also unmeasured.

(4) Tier I: 0.

(5) Stages: Stage 1 assumes about 92% of the 6-market shortlist is already found by US/UK/AU (unmeasured).

(6) Monthly:
- 300 new places: 300 × 2.565 = 770 keywords → 1 task per market → 0.54; LLM 0.08; Tier Q 300 × 0.773 × 0.33 × (0.002 + 0.3 × 0.00225) = 0.205.
- Drain capped at 1.00.
- Amortised refreshes: 10.2/6 + 5.0/12.

Every figure is an upper bound on scope, because the C1 exclusion of inactive, transit, unnamed and orphan places is not yet measured. The 0.09 price for a full 1,000-keyword task has not been seen live (largest seen: 395). Jev decide() calls and Cohere embeddings at recompute are not costed.

name: Approach B: a per-tour SEO pack (tour × market) built for free from one place-level purchase store
summary:
Today the same Google data is bought in two shapes: per tour by S1 (written to seo_context, US only, hidden from everyone else) and per place × market by segment research (written to search_demand, hidden from S1, T8, T9 and quarter-plan). Writers read whichever store their code was wired to, so T2 for a UK/DE tenant falls back to US keywords, T8/T9 get nothing for any tour S1 never fetched, and the Slate never sees research until an unrelated recompute runs.

Approach B splits buying from consuming:
(1) ONE BUYER, at place level. The `seo_research` job (a rework of segment_research) buys in full batches: volumes for every mapped keyword × every target market in 1,000-keyword tasks; ONE SERP per place, US location / English only, giving PAA + related searches + organic domains; keywords_for_keywords off by default. Everything it buys lands in acp_contract.search_demand. A new acp_contract.place_keyword_map persists the Haiku keyword proposals, so a second market or a refresh never pays the LLM again, and the pack builder can join on exact keywords instead of ILIKE.
(2) ONE WRITER UNIT, the tour pack. A new acp_contract.tour_seo_pack holds one row per (tour, market) for the 6 markets: 892 × 6 ≈ 5,352 rows. It is derived for free from map + search_demand by services/seo_intelligence/tour_pack.py. It carries top_keywords with volume and places, keyword_by_place, PAA with its source keyword and market, related_keywords, max_volume and relevance bucket, coverage counts, a status (ok / thin / empty) and a fingerprint. A debounced job rebuilds a pack after research, after any atomize or tour recompute, and on a nightly fingerprint sweep. The pack has no TTL of its own; freshness belongs to the purchases underneath it.
(3) EVERY WRITER READS PACKS.
- S1 (process_seo / s1_seo_prefetch / s1_batch) reads the AA-market pack and stops buying per tour. A thin pack sends that tour's places to the research queue; it does not trigger a per-tour keywords_for_keywords call.
- T2 reads the packs of all of the tenant's markets (plural, proxies allowed). It takes PAA from any English market and keeps only source-covered keywords (S1 v2 relevant_keywords), so the validate DFS_INTENT_UNDERUSED −1.0 never fires on a forced query.
- T8 and T9 read the pack for (tour, tenant market). T9 picks its SEO keyword from keyword_by_place for the piece's own places.
- Quarter-plan dfs_relevance reads pack.max_volume.
- Ranking keeps reading search_demand directly, because a Segment spans tours and the place-level store is the aggregate.
- The Slate Blog bar takes MAX demand across the tenant's markets instead of the demand of the best-rank market, and reports no-data vs below-bar.
(4) A COMPLETED RESEARCH RUN TRIGGERS THE NEXT STEPS. Each successful run enqueues one debounced platform recompute (segment_ids = the researched Segments) plus a pack rebuild for the affected tours. A daily read-only guard reports the stale share per market from the v_research_due view and opens an issue above a threshold (AA-1055).

COST at the rates measured 08/11, all 6 default markets, first pass ≈ 22.8 USD (≈17.4 with a SERP gate of volume ≥100). That is 10.17 volumes + 1.85 LLM keyword map + 10.76 SERP. The ceiling is ≈35. Today's design over the same scope: ≈80–95.
Recommended order, each phase approved separately:
- Phase 0 (0 USD): code changes, plus a free backfill of the existing S1 seo_context keyword ideas and PAA into search_demand and the keyword map, which recovers the ~16.65 USD of October purchases.
- Phase 1: US+UK+AU, ≈17.7 USD. Leaves ≈9.8 of the 27.41 balance.
- Phase 2: DE/FR/NL, volumes only, ≈5.1 USD, because the PAA was already bought once in US/en.
Steady state: ≈1.1 USD per monthly incremental run (≈300 new places assumed). On top of that, a ≈10 USD volume refresh every 182 days (first one due ~May 2027) and a ≈11 USD PAA refresh every 365 days. That averages ≈3.7 USD/month and needs a DFS top-up before May 2027.
A full S1 catalogue rerun stops buying DFS: today it costs 13–82 USD, under this design 0. T2/T7/T8/T9 stay at 0.

Where B is weaker than a pure 'one store, no pack' design (approach A):
- The pack is one more derived table, and it can go stale if a rebuild fails. Mitigation: the reader builds the pack inline on a miss or a fingerprint mismatch, which is cheap and free.
- For ranking and the Slate, 'aggregated packs' would be the wrong grain, so B deliberately leaves them on search_demand.
B's gain: every writer gets one stable per-tour object for its market, with a coverage status the UI can show. S1, T2, T8 and T9 then share one loader instead of four ad-hoc queries.

Layers and their lifetimes:
- Keyword map (place → keywords). Persistent, versioned by prompt_version. It is re-proposed only for a NEW or RENAMED canonical_place, or when the prompt version is bumped by hand.
- Volumes (search_demand.retrieved_on). Fresh for 182 days (FRESH_FOR, unchanged). Google Ads volumes are 12-month averages, so twice a year is enough.
- PAA, related searches and SERP domains. Fresh for 365 days, tracked in a new search_demand.paa_retrieved_on column, separate from volume freshness.
- segment_research_log becomes per (place, market, tier), so volume-fresh and PAA-fresh can differ.
- Tour packs have NO TTL. They are derived from the layers above. Each pack stores a fingerprint: a hash of the tour's active atom places + its title places + the max retrieved_on / paa_retrieved_on of the rows it used + PACK_VERSION.

Pack rebuild triggers (all free, debounced job `tour_seo_pack_build`):
- (a) A research run completes: rebuild packs for every tour that contains a researched place.
- (b) An a3_atomize job or a scope=tour recompute completes: rebuild that tour's packs. Its new or renamed places appear in v_research_due right away.
- (c) The segment stage merges a Segment or writes an alias: rebuild the packs of the affected tours.
- (d) A nightly sweep rebuilds packs whose fingerprint no longer matches.
- (e) Read-through: a reader that finds no pack, or a mismatched one, builds it inline and upserts it.

Research (paid) triggers. Nothing buys automatically; every run is approved:
- Re-atomize and renames feed v_research_due: places of active tours (v_active_tour_atoms, minus transit, unnamed and orphan places via resolve_exclusions) with no fresh volume row for a target market, or no fresh PAA. This matches AA-1055: 'a re-atomize queues its places, no paid call until approved'.
- A monthly incremental run is proposed from v_research_due with a cost preview and a monthly cap.
- Full volume refresh every 182 days, PAA refresh every 365 days, each a separately approved run. The first volume refresh after this pass is due ~May 2027.
- Before an S1 wave, the admin can run a scoped research pass over the wave's tours (tour_ids scope). A thin pack is the signal for this.

Recompute link: every successful research run calls enqueue_recompute(scope='platform', segment_ids=<Segments of researched places>, debounce_s=180). The existing coalescing (recompute_job.py:70-116) folds bursts together, so new demand reaches atom_ranking and the Slate within minutes.

- It computes the stale share per market (places due / places in scope) and the pack coverage (share of active tours whose pack for a tenant market is ok / thin / empty).
- It opens or updates one issue above a threshold, using the root CI-hygiene pattern.

- LLM = 0.039/154 = 0.000253 USD per place.
- Volume task = 0.09 USD per ≤1,000 keywords per market.
- SERP = 0.002 USD per call.
Volumes per market = ceil(stale × k / 1000) × 0.09:
- US 6,962 × 2.565 = 17,858 keywords → 18 tasks = 1.62.
- UK and AU 7,145 → 18,327 → 19 tasks = 1.71 each.
- DE, FR and NL 7,243 → 18,578 → 19 tasks = 1.71 each.
- Total 1.62 + 5 × 1.71 = 10.17.
LLM keyword map, once for all markets: 7,323 × 0.000253 = 1.85. Ceiling: 0.28 per 200 places = 10.25.

cost_check:
The expected-case arithmetic is correct. The ceiling is not.

EXPECTED CASE (I recomputed it from the live facts and the code):
- Volumes: US ceil(6,962×2.565/1000)=18 tasks; UK/AU ceil(7,145×2.565/1000)=19 each; DE/FR/NL ceil(7,243×2.565/1000)=19 each. That is 113 tasks × 0.09 = 10.17.
- SERP: 7,323 × 0.773 × 0.002 = 11.32. The 77.3% share matches the code: SERP_KEYWORDS_PER_PLACE=1 and only keywords with volume above 0 get a SERP (segment_research_batch.py:66, :316-324).
- LLM: 7,323 × 0.039/154 = 1.85.
- Total: DFS 21.49 + LLM 1.85 = 23.35. The design says 23.4, so this is correct.
- R1 checks out: 1.86 + (18+19+19)×0.09 = 5.04. R3 checks out: 57×0.09 = 5.13.
- Gated variant: 10.17 + 5.66 + 1.86 = 17.7. It rests on an unmeasured 50% share.

THE CEILING IS WRONG (understated):
- The design gives a DFS ceiling of 24.8 = 10.17 + 14.65. That reuses the measured 2.565 keywords per place, but the code allows KEYWORDS_PER_PLACE=4 (:52).
- The real volume ceiling is ceil(6,962×4/1000)=28 + 5×29 = 173 tasks = 15.57.
- The real DFS ceiling is 15.57 + 14.65 = 30.2. That is MORE than the 27.41 balance, before the unexplained off-ledger drop of 0.7-1.5.
- The 2.565 rate came from 154 US places that had already been researched on 25/09, when the run averaged 4.5 keywords per place. DE/FR/NL have only 263 rows each in the store, so they will see fewer volume cache hits. The real rate for those markets may sit above 2.565.
- Conclusion: a one-shot 6-market pass is not safe within the balance. It needs a pre-run balance check (the client already has appendix_user_data, which is free) and a hard USD gate with a reserve.

UNCOSTED, AND IT CAN STOP THE RUN:
- _gate_keywords sends every non-plain keyword to Jev decide(). That is roughly 7,323 × 1.6-3 = 12k-22k calls, billed on input tokens.
- Jev has a hard daily budget (decide.py:755-808). If it trips mid-pass, the guard aborts the remaining places.
- The design lists Jev as "not costed". That is not acceptable for a cost-first plan. The calls need an estimate, and they need to be split across days or covered by the persisted jev_ok column.

BASELINE "TODAY 80-97" IS SHAKY IN BOTH DIRECTIONS:
- It overstates the LLM line: one run already takes several markets and proposes keywords once per run, not 6 times.
- It understates volumes: MAX_PLACES_PER_RUN=200 forces about 37 runs. Each run pays at least 1 task per market, so today's code would cost 37×6 = 222 tasks = 20.0 for volumes, not 10.17.
- The direction of the conclusion still holds: today's design costs much more.

BIGGEST MISSED LEVER (my prices from memory, not verified; check dataforseo.com/pricing before relying on them):
- Every call uses /live endpoints (dataforseo_client.py:254, 300, 350, 454).
- DataForSEO's Standard queue (task_post + tasks_ready + task_get, all free to poll) is cheaper. For serp/organic/advanced at normal priority I recall about 0.0006 per SERP against 0.002 live. Google Ads search_volume Standard is roughly 2/3 of the live price.
- This work is an offline batch with nobody waiting, so latency does not matter.
- Estimate on those prices: SERP 5,661 × 0.0006 = 3.4 instead of 11.3. Volumes about 6.8 instead of 10.2. DFS first pass about 10 USD instead of 21.5. Monthly SERP refresh roughly a third of the design's figure.

MONTHLY:
- 3.6/month recomputes correctly: 2.16 + 0.46 + 0.94 + 0.08.
- A 182-day volume refresh buys little. Google Ads search_volume is a trailing 12-month average, so a 365-day refresh would halve that line, to about 1.1.
flaws: The stated ceiling (DFS 24.8 / all-in 35.1) reuses the measured 2.565 keywords per place. The code allows KEYWORDS_PER_PLACE=4. The real DFS ceiling is about 30.2 USD, which exceeds the 27.41 balance. The design presents the full pass as fitting the balance, but only the expected case does.

Jev decide() keyword gating (about 12k-22k calls over 7,323 places) is left uncosted. Its hard daily budget can abort a large pass partway, and the partial-run behaviour is not designed. In a cost-first plan both the spend and the stop risk have to be in the estimate.

It never considers DataForSEO's Standard queue (task_post/task_get) instead of /live. Every buy is an offline batch, and the queue plausibly cuts the SERP line by about 70% and volumes by about 1/3, roughly halving the 21.5 USD pass. It is the largest unit-economics lever and it is missing. Prices are from memory and must be verified.

It spends 5.13 USD on DE/FR/NL volumes for keywords proposed in English, with the language defaulting to 'en' (seed_builder.py:437). The likely result is mostly zero or tiny numbers. With the new MAX-across-markets bar they rarely change any decision, and every tenant is a Dev demo tenant (no real users). The value per dollar is the lowest of any line, yet it is in the default pass.

The optional SERP gate at volume >=100 (saving 5.66) contradicts the audit's own evidence. Place PAA feeds Route FAQs and T2 below that bar (real_questions.py:9-12, 386-411). Offering it as a cost option without that warning invites a false saving.

Google Ads Keyword Planner (free) is not evaluated, although the brief asked for it. Constraints: an Ads account, developer-token approval at Basic access (a test token returns fake data), bucketed ranges for accounts without spend, and quota. It could only replace the volume line (about 10 USD first pass, about 2 USD a month), so it is probably not worth the effort at this scale, but the design should say so.

The 'today 80-97 USD' comparison is mis-built. It counts 6 separate LLM proposals although one run already handles several markets, and it ignores the 200-place cap, which multiplies volume tasks to about 222 (about 20 USD). The conclusion holds, but the figure is not defensible as written.

The SERP estimate does not subtract places that already have PAA from 25/09 or 08/11 (about 540 places, about 1.1 USD), even though its own skip-if-fresh rule would. The figure is slightly high, not wrong.

The rolling 182-day volume refresh is over-frequent for a trailing 12-month average. A 365-day refresh, with no refresh for markets that have no paying tenant, brings steady state to about 1.5 USD a month instead of 3.6.

Simplicity cost: 3 new tables (place_keyword, research_plan, new search_demand columns) plus a new demand_profile module, plus seam changes in S1, T2, Slate, dfs_relevance, recompute and debate in one design. That is a large risky-class change set. For DFS savings alone, the core is just 'one buyer + one SERP per place + no cap + persisted map'.
strengths: One SERP per place, in a single English market, instead of one per market with volume. This removes the largest repeated cost (up to 6×11.3 USD) and also harvests related_searches and organic domains from the same paid call at no extra cost.

Removing MAX_PLACES_PER_RUN=200 and packing full 1,000-keyword tasks per market cuts volume tasks from about 222 to 113. The minimum-of-one-task-per-market floor is correctly identified as the reason to batch monthly, never weekly.
A persisted place->keyword map with a jev_ok column means the LLM proposal and the Jev gate are paid once per place across all markets and every refresh, not once per run.

S1 and T2 become read-only consumers of the store. This ends per-tour keywords_for_keywords + SERP buys (0.092 USD per tour, up to about 82 USD per full-catalogue rerun). Tiers in a stable order: volumes, then questions, then ideas (off).

Ledger tags (job_id, reason) and a standing monthly cap fix the 25/09-style untraceable 49 USD spend.
steal: Move every batch buy to DataForSEO's Standard queue (task_post, then poll tasks_ready, then task_get; polling is free) for search_volume and serp/organic/advanced. Verify the live prices first. If the SERP is about 0.0006, the first pass falls to about 10 USD DFS and the gated variant becomes pointless.

Pre-run balance check through the existing appendix_user_data call (free). Abort or shrink the plan when the ceiling plus a reserve (for example 3 USD) exceeds the balance. Compute the ceiling with KEYWORDS_PER_PLACE=4, not the measured 2.565.

cost_check:
I recomputed the cost from the live facts. The arithmetic in the design is right, but some of the framing around it is wrong.

Volume tasks per market are ceil(stale x 2.565 / 1000): US 6,962 needs 18 tasks; UK/AU 7,145 and DE/FR/NL 7,243 need 19 each. That is 113 tasks x 0.09 = 10.17 USD.

SERP, one per place, is 7,323 x 0.773 x 0.002 = 11.32 USD, so DFS comes to 21.49. The LLM keyword map is 7,323 x 0.000253 = 1.85, so pass 1 is about 23.35 USD all-in (the design says 23.4). With the >=100 gate it is 15.83 DFS + 1.85 = 17.7. The ceiling is 10.17 + 14.65 SERP + 10.25 LLM = 35.1, matching the design. The staged runs also check out: R1 is 56 tasks = 5.04, R3 is 57 tasks = 5.13, R1+R2+R3 DFS = 21.5.

Caveats the number hides:
1. The 77.3% SERP rate was measured on US volume only. Code shows the old path bought one SERP per place per market with volume (SERP_KEYWORDS_PER_PLACE=1), so 119/154 is a US-only share. With a union over US/UK/AU volumes the share can only rise, toward the 14.65 ceiling. A realistic DFS figure is 21.5-24.8.
2. Jev decide() is not costed. _gate_keywords runs on every proposed keyword, about 29k for 7,323 places at 4 per place. It needs a number before approval.
3. The country x activity keyword set adds keywords, about +1 partial task per market (up to +0.54).
4. Balance: 27.41 - 21.5 leaves 5.9 before the unexplained off-ledger drain (about 0.7-1.5 seen over about 2 weeks). After the drain it is about 4.4-5.2, and about 2.6 in the ceiling case.

Monthly: the arithmetic is right too: 2.16 + 0.46 + 0.94 + 0.08 = 3.64 USD. But the derived due list (expiry at FRESH_FOR = 182 days) cannot produce 'rolling 1/6 per month'. Pass 1 stamps about 7k places within a day or two, so months 1-5 cost about 1.1 (new places only) and month 6 has a cliff of about 10.2 volumes. Month 12 adds about 11.3 PAA on top. The annual total is about the same (about 40-44 USD), but cash flow is lumpy. Smoothing it means refreshing early by choice, which the design does not specify. The 80-97 USD comparison against today's design is consistent: 6 x 1.86 + 10.17 + 6 x 11.32 + 84 x 0.09 = 97.4.
flaws: The phases and the freshness log clash. research_batch writes segment_research_log once per (place, market), at the END of all phases, for places that did not fail. With selectable phases, R1 (volumes only) either marks places fresh, so R2 cannot use the log to pick SERP places, or it does not, so R2 re-enters the volume phase. The design needs a separate questions-due selector (no fresh paa_retrieved_on), and the log semantics must be defined per phase.

PAA freshness is missing from the due list. research_due is defined as 'no fresh log row OR no keyword map', but PAA has its own 365-day clock on a new column. As written, the PAA refresh (0.94 USD/month line) is never scheduled. Existing PAA rows also have no paa_retrieved_on, so the migration needs a backfill rule: copy retrieved_on, or treat them as stale.

The 'rolling' refresh is not real. A derived 'expired after 182d' list plus a one-shot pass gives an expiry cliff at month 6 (about 10.2 USD) and month 12 (+11.3 PAA), not 3.6 USD/month. Readers do not filter on retrieved_on (checked: atom_ranking, slate, real_questions, s1_prefetch), so the Slate does not collapse. But the monthly cap (suggested 5) will block the month-6 plan, and nobody has said what happens then.

The balance check blocks small runs long before money runs out. segment_research_job.run refuses when balance < dfs_budget.remaining_usd(), comparing against the budget, not the estimate. After pass 1 the balance is about 4.4-5.9. With a 5 USD monthly cap, the first 1.1 USD monthly run fails NonRetryable even though it would fit. The design adds a monthly cap without fixing this comparison.

The standing monthly allowance brings back auto-spend. DFS gets bought with no human click, which is the exact failure class of 25/09 that the audit's root cause #1 and the reference README forbid. It is also unclear who fires the run on the 1st: there is no named scheduler, and the 'approve plan' and 'standing allowance' paths overlap. The design should pick one. For a 1-2 person team, the safer pick is a click-to-approve plan with a cap.

The approval and run scope can drift. The pending research_plan is upserted again by every A3/place job. If the job runs over the derived due list at run time, an approved 2 USD plan can run on more places than were approved. Approval must freeze a place snapshot plus a USD cap, and the job must run (snapshot ∩ still due) under that cap. Concurrent upserts from parallel atomize jobs also need a unique partial index on status='pending'.

refresh_plan() runs in the A3/place job hot path. It is a derived SQL over v_active_tour_atoms x log x 6 markets, executed at the end of every a3_atomize, and an S1/A3 wave atomizes hundreds of tours. It must be best-effort (never fail the atomize), debounced, or moved to a single deferred job. The design says none of this.

Runtime blocks deploys, and the job is not resumable. A full pass is about 489 sequential Haiku calls (_propose has no concurrency), about 29k Jev gates at concurrency 8, 113 volume tasks and about 5.7-7.3k live SERPs at SERP_CONCURRENCY=4. That is a multi-hour job (realistically 3-6h) against expected_seconds=3600, with concurrency=1 and max_attempts=2, and the debounced platform recompute comes on top. Under DM-11.4 it blocks every CIS backend deploy and DB Migrate apply for the whole window. The design does not say how to chunk it or whether the kind is deploy_gate_exempt.

Prefetch contends with admin runs. s1_seo_prefetch becomes run_segment_research(tour_ids), but segment_research is a concurrency=1 job kind. A wave prefetch either queues behind a multi-hour admin pass, stalling the S1 wave, or bypasses the job lock and loses the single-buyer guarantee. The design gives no rule.

The T2 ordering gate is enforced only by prose. R1 volumes become visible to T2 at once, because tenant_market_seo reads search_demand directly with no recompute in between. So the relevant_keywords PR must be deployed BEFORE R1, or DFS_INTENT_UNDERUSED (-1.0) switches on. This should be a hard gate (a flag or version check on the run endpoint), not a note.

Too many Slate behaviour changes land together. New demand data, the MAX-demand Blog bar, the English-only questions_count filter and the contested writer all change Blog output. 'Recompute then measure Blog coverage' cannot attribute the effect of each. The English-only filter also invalidates questions_count across the board, so the first recompute is a full re-landing, not the limited one the design claims.

Gates and moving parts are heavy for a 1-2 person team. The design adds 1 migration (3 objects: place_keyword, research_plan, 3 new search_demand columns), 3 new modules, about 15 changed files, an admin page and plan approval. Spending is guarded by per-run budget + daily budget + monthly cap + balance check + plan approval. Most of this is not needed to approve the first runs.

Some cost lines are missing or unmeasured: Jev decide() over about 29k keywords, the union SERP share across 3 English markets, billing for a 1,000-keyword task (never seen above 395), and the off-ledger DFS drain, which should be found before automating anything. The '>=100 gate = 50%' figure is assumed, though R1 measures it for free.

The proxy map (CA→US, SG/HK/AE→UK, NZ→AU) is presented as 'labelled'. But the Slate reason, T2 seo_source and the admin pages each need that label, and only T2 gets a concrete label set. The tenant-facing wording is unspecified, and memory says tenants see content only, so it must stay internal/admin.
strengths: There is a single buyer, and every writer (S1, T2, T7, T8, T9, A3) reads the store. That closes the per-tour S1 purchase path: 13-82 USD per full rerun, and the October spend source.

The arithmetic is correct and honestly labelled. It separates expected cost from the ceiling, puts the figures next to today's design (about 97), and runs in stages (R1 free-measures the >=100 share before R2).

The due list is derived instead of queued, so a rename, dedupe or re-atomize becomes due automatically with no queue to drift. A crashed run resumes cheaply, because volumes are cache-checked and place_keyword stops repeat LLM spend.

Research is coupled to the Slate through the existing enqueue_recompute sliding debounce (AA-743), and _store_paa already invalidates questions_count per keyword. That fixes the 'paid research invisible to Slate' gap with code that already exists.
One English SERP per place matches how the data is consumed: T9 already drops non-English PAA, and the place_paa tier reads any market. It saves about 5 x 11 USD against SERP per market.
It reuses atom_ranking.resolve_exclusions for scope, so money stops going to places the Slate already excludes.
It flags the T2 DFS_INTENT_UNDERUSED penalty switch-on risk and the absolute 1,000 Blog bar as decisions for the tech lead.
steal: Split the pass into jobs per phase: (1) map + volumes for all 6 markets, as one fast job of about 113 tasks with no packing loss; (2) SERP in chunks of about 1,000 places (SERP is per keyword, so chunking costs nothing). This keeps each job under about 1h, frees deploy windows between chunks, and makes R2 resumable.

Write freshness per phase: segment_research_log for volumes per (place, market), paa_retrieved_on per keyword for questions, and two due selectors behind one /due endpoint. Backfill paa_retrieved_on = retrieved_on in the migration.
Drop the research_plan table: make approval = POST run with a frozen place snapshot + max_usd, created from the free GET /due preview. shared.job already holds status, payload and cost.
Fix the balance gate to compare against the run's ESTIMATE (or max_usd), not the budget's remaining amount. Otherwise small monthly runs fail once the balance drops below the cap.
Hard gate: the research run endpoint refuses markets beyond the audit scope until the T2 relevant_keywords change is deployed (a feature flag checked at enqueue).

Smooth the refresh on purpose: each monthly run also takes the oldest N places (about 1/6) even when not yet expired, or the month-6 cliff is accepted as its own approved run. Pick one and write it down.
No standing auto-spend in the dev phase: the daily stale-share guard opens or updates an issue with the free estimate, and a human clicks. Keep the monthly cap only as a ceiling.

Ship in this order to keep effects attributable: scope filter + one-SERP-per-place + recompute enqueue + T2 filter → R1/R2 + recompute → measure → then the MAX-demand bar → then contested in shadow, with S1 read-only last after the 3-tour trial.
Find the off-ledger DFS drain (about 0.7-1.5 USD) and measure Jev cost per keyword before approving pass 1. Plan a DFS top-up right after pass 1, not 'within 2 months'.

cost_check:
I recomputed the cost from the live facts and the design's arithmetic holds. Volumes: US ceil(6,962×2.565/1000)=18 tasks, and UK/AU/DE/FR/NL ceil(~18.3k–18.6k/1000)=19 tasks each, so 113 tasks × 0.09 = 10.17. SERP: 7,323 × 0.773 × 0.002 = 11.32 (ceiling 14.65). LLM keyword map: 7,323 × 0.000253 = 1.85. Pass 1 = 21.49 DFS + 1.85 LLM = 23.3 USD all-in. Ceiling = 24.82 DFS + 10.25 LLM ≈ 35.1. Monthly: 24 volume tasks 2.16 + 232 new SERPs 0.46 + 472 PAA refresh 0.94 + 0.08 LLM = 3.64 USD. The design's numbers are right.

What they leave out, and why they are low or skewed:
(1) Jev (TypeSafe, paid, with a daily cap in cost_guard) is not costed. The post-research platform recompute calls decide() for a3_demand_belongs (up to 3 per Segment moment × new keyword), for country-scope per (country set, question), and for landing per (moment, question). Roughly 22k new PAA questions across 11,594 Segments could mean tens of thousands of decide calls. That can trip the jev daily cap and leave the recompute half done. It is the largest unpriced line.
(2) The country×activity keyword set adds 0–1 volume task per market (0–0.54).
(3) The SERP share could exceed 77% once any of 6 markets counts as 'has volume'. Use 14.65 as the planning number, not 11.32.
(4) The 80–97 USD 'today's design' comparison is a strawman. It assumes ideas are on and a full per-market SERP in DE/FR/NL, where Asian place names rarely have volume. A fair baseline (suggestions off, 6 LLM proposals, SERP only where a market has volume) is about 45–55 USD, so the real saving is about 25–30 USD per full pass, not 60–75.
(5) 21.5 DFS of the 27.41 balance leaves about 5.9 USD, below one ceiling-case overrun (+3.3 SERP). R2 should be quoted after R1, as the design proposes.

Planning figure: about 23 USD expected, about 27 DFS + Jev unknown as a safe ceiling.
flaws: S1 coverage gap for NEW tours (chicken-and-egg). S1 runs before A3 atomize (S1 rewrite → review/Master → atomize), but the research scope and the derived due list both come from v_active_tour_atoms. A tour that has never been atomized has no atom places, so it never becomes 'due', the wave-scoped s1_seo_prefetch run finds nothing, and demand_profile only has title words. Today process_seo buys title-seeded keyword ideas before atomize. Under this design, every newly onboarded tour (the source of the assumed ~300 new places a month) gets an S1 rewrite with no SEO at all. The design says 'S1 proceeds with what it has', which for new tours means nothing.

demand_profile matches on ILIKE '%term%' name overlap (inherited from tenant_market_seo), with no ownership check. Ranking needs the Jev a3_demand_belongs verdict to stop 'Kyoto' 165k being claimed by 'Kyoto incense-making'. The profile has no such check, so S1/T2 get over-broad head terms and the HIGH relevance bucket (quarter plan, T8) is inflated. The design builds a persisted place_keyword map but does not say demand_profile joins through it. It should.

related_searches only exist for SERPs bought from now on, and the rule 'skip SERP when any market has PAA < 365 days' blocks the backfill. Places researched on 28/09 or 08/11 (the audit tenant's 154, the hottest ones) keep PAA but get no related_searches for a year. Those are exactly the places T8's related block and T9's choose_keyword need. The skip rule must also check related_searches IS NOT NULL.

The materialised seo_context payload lists top_keywords, people_also_ask and related_keywords, but not keyword_ideas with search_volume. dfs_relevance (quarter plan relevance and the T8 relevance bucket) computes its bucket from keyword_ideas volumes. The seo_context fallback path would score every tour MED. Also, seo_context.expires_at is 7 days today, so the T8 rule 'fall back when expired' fires for essentially every existing row, an inconsistency the design does not address.

Overwriting the October S1 seo_context rows (title-seeded keywords_for_keywords phrases like 'bhutan cultural tour') with place-level profiles is a silent quality regression for S1/T2/T8. The design mentions a 3-tour trial but does not say 'merge, never replace existing tour-level ideas'.

T2 language/market mismatch. T2 takes a free-form rewrite_language. A DE/FR/NL tenant writing in German gets English place keywords (volumes measured in the DE location). relevant_keywords checks coverage against the English source, so they pass the filter, yet they will never appear in a German seo_title. DFS_INTENT_UNDERUSED (-1.0) then fires anyway. The claim 'content is written in English' is true for T9/S1 but not proven for T2.

PAA market fidelity for T2. The one English SERP per place goes to the market with max volume, nearly always US. UK/AU tenants (8 of the declarations, the largest group) get US PAA, such as visa or flight questions phrased for US travellers, in their FAQ and T2 input. This is accepted as a risk, but no per-tenant opt-in is costed.

Recompute after a full pass is not 'bounded'. _store_paa invalidates questions_count for every candidate Segment of every keyword whose PAA changed. A 5,600-SERP pass therefore NULLs most of the 11,594 Segments, and precompute_question_landings re-embeds and re-decides almost the whole platform. The docstring of that function records runs of 6–16 hours. The job-idle rule (DM-11.4) then blocks deploys or migrations for that window. Jev cost and cap are not addressed.

The country×activity keywords have no place, but place_keyword's PK is (canonical_place, keyword). That is a schema mismatch, or else they are duplicated per place and over-claimed by name-match in ranking.

Scope creep makes the change hard to review and roll back. It bundles 1 migration (2 new tables + 3 columns), about 15 files across S1, T2, T7, T8, the quarter plan, ranking, recompute, the Debate contested writer, admin API + UI, and a watch job. The contested writer and the English-only PAA filter are independent ranking changes that alter Slate output, and they ride along. 'No new queue table' is cosmetic: research_plan is a stateful queue with status transitions.

The ordering dependency 'T2 filter must ship before pass-1 data' is real but understated. T2 already receives tenant-market keywords today, plus the admin US fallback for every tour S1 rewrote in October, so the -1.0 penalty is already live. The filter is a fix needed now, not a gate in front of pass 1.
Tenant-owned tours (owner_scope tenant) and unpublished raw tours are out of scope, so their T2/T9 runs get no data. The design accepts this, but it contradicts 'every writer gets the data it needs'.
strengths: One buyer and one store. Every writer reads the store and nothing else, enforced with an import-guard test. This closes the 25/09 failure class for good.
One English SERP per place instead of one per market. It is the biggest structural saving, and it is correct because question landing in A3 is market-independent and T9 already drops non-English PAA.
Volumes are packed into full 1,000-keyword tasks for all 6 markets (about 1.7 USD per market). The cheap signal is bought broadly and the expensive one narrowly.
A persisted place→keyword map removes the 6× repeat of the LLM proposal and makes refreshes nearly free in LLM cost.
A derived due list over v_active_tour_atoms minus segment_research_log. It cannot drift, and re-atomize, rename or dedupe make places due automatically.
Research enqueues a debounced platform recompute. That fixes the measured gap (4 → 31 Blog-eligible only after a manual recompute).

The Slate Blog bar reads MAX demand across the tenant's markets, with no_data and below_bar split. This fixes a real bug (verified in slate.py:272-300: the best-rank market wins even when its demand is null).
T2 reads plural tenant markets, a labelled proxy map (CA/NZ/SG/HK/AE) and PAA from any English market, so 7 currently dropped agency declarations become covered.
Cost arithmetic checks out. Staged R0 (free) → R1 → quote → R2 → R3, with each stage priced, fits the approval-first rule.
A two-number estimate (expected at measured rates plus a ceiling) replaces the estimate_cost figure, which reads about 2× high.
steal: Keep these from the design: one English SERP per place's best keyword, volumes in full tasks for all 6 markets, the persisted place_keyword map, the derived due list, and the debounced recompute after research.

Make demand_profile join place→keyword through place_keyword, plus the cached a3_demand_belongs Jev verdicts. Do not use ILIKE name overlap. Writers then get the same ownership-checked keywords that ranking uses.

Fix the S1 new-tour hole. Seed the wave-scoped research run from the tour's extracted places (place_extract / tour_spec title + itinerary places), not only from v_active_tour_atoms. Or keep a capped per-tour title-seed keywords_for_keywords call (full 20-seed tasks batched across the wave) for tours with zero atoms only.
Skip a SERP only when PAA, related_searches and serp_domains are all fresh. Backfill related_searches for already-researched high-volume places in R2.

Materialise seo_context with keyword_ideas (keyword + search_volume) so dfs_relevance's fallback still buckets. Merge with existing tour-level ideas, never overwrite. Make T8's fallback key on 'missing', not on the 7-day expires_at.

Price and cap Jev for the post-research recompute: a dry count of new (moment, question) and (moment, keyword) pairs in R0, a temporary jev/recompute budget row, and recompute run by market or by chunk so it can resume.

Ship in thin slices: (1) T2 relevant_keywords filter + Slate MAX/no_data split + import guard (no migration); (2) migration + scope filter + one-SERP-per-place + research→recompute; (3) demand_profile for S1/T2/T8; (4) contested writer and English-only PAA as separate shadowed PRs.
Gate T2 keywords by rewrite_language. Pass DFS keywords only when the rewrite language is English, or label them 'context only' so DFS_INTENT_UNDERUSED does not fire for non-English rewrites.
Allow a per-tenant opt-in UK/AU SERP (0.002 per keyword) for the top-N Blog-relevant places of a paying UK/AU tenant, instead of the US PAA serving everyone.

cost_check:
I recomputed the design's numbers from the live facts. The arithmetic is right, but the price basis is the most expensive DFS mode.

Tier V, packed volumes, one ceil(stale × 2.565 / 1000) × 0.09 per market:
- US: 17,858 keywords → 18 tasks → 1.62.
- UK and AU: 18,327 → 19 → 1.71 each.
- DE, FR and NL: 18,578 → 19 → 1.71 each.
- Total 10.17. This matches the design.

LLM: 7,323 × 0.000253 = 1.85. Matches.

Tier Q, shortlist central 1,868 places: 1,868 × 0.002 = 3.74, plus 30% depth-2 retries 1,868 × 0.3 × 0.00225 = 1.26, so 5.00 (range 3.79–6.06). Matches.

Totals: first pass 17.0, Stage 1 = 5.04 + 1.85 + 4.6 = 11.49, Stage 2 = 5.13 + 0.4 = 5.53. Monthly: 0.54 + 0.08 + 0.205 = 0.82, plus a drain of at most 1.0, so 0.8–1.8. Amortised 1.7 + 0.42 + monthly ≈ 3.0–3.9. All match.

Design A cross-check: 10.17 + 5,661 × 0.002 + 1.85 = 23.3. Matches.

Where the numbers are wrong or soft:

(1) The hard ceiling of 26.5 is not derived and is too low. The true worst case is:
- Tier V with all 4 keywords per place: 2.52 (US) + 5 × 2.61 = 15.6.
- A shortlist that swallows every place with volume: 5,661 × (0.002 + 0.3 × 0.00225) = 15.1.
- That gives about 30.8 USD DFS, above the 27.41 balance, and about 39.7 if every place retries.
- The 22 USD run cap keeps the balance safe, but a cap hit leaves a half-done Tier Q. So Tier V must finish for every market before Tier Q starts.

(2) The 0.09 price for a full 1,000-keyword task is unverified.
- cost_guard.py:44-46 records the task price rising with keyword count: 0.057 for 13 keywords or fewer, 0.09 for about 150, 0.09 at 395.
- If it rises again past 395, Tier V moves. The first task of the run should be a 1,000-keyword probe that aborts above about 0.10.

(3) Every client call is a /live endpoint.
- Both calls go to /live: search_volume (dataforseo_client.py:300) and serp/google/organic/live/advanced (:350).
- From memory of DFS public pricing, so check on the price page: SERP is about 0.0006 in the standard queue (task_post) and 0.0012 at priority, against 0.002 live. Google Ads search_volume is about 0.05 standard against about 0.075–0.09 live.
- Research is an offline admin batch, so the standard queue fits. Same scope at standard rates:
  - Tier V: 113 tasks × about 0.055 ≈ 6.2.
  - Tier Q: 1,868 × 0.0006 plus retries ≈ 1.5.
  - DFS total about 7.7 against 15.2.
- Even design A (a SERP for every place with volume) would then cost 5,661 × 0.0006 ≈ 3.4 plus retries, about 4.5. That is cheaper than design C's live shortlist (5.0).
- The live-vs-queue price choice moves more money than the shortlist does.

(4) The design's saving over design A is only about 6.3 USD, one time (23.3 − 17.0). It buys that with 4 new tables, a two-pass order dependency, and a tenant-fed purchase queue.

(5) DE/FR/NL Tier V (5.13) buys English-language volumes. resolve_buyer_markets passes 'en' to every market (seed_builder.py:53,61). In those markets this undercounts systematically, so the money buys poor data.
- Two cheaper options: drop language_code for non-English markets (no cost; check the DFS docs), or have Stage 2 buy only the keywords that showed volume in US/UK/AU.
- At a guessed 40% non-zero share, that is about 7.4k keywords, 8 tasks, 0.72 per market: about 2.2 instead of 5.13.

(6) Shortlist share 25–40% is a guess, and the units don't match. It compares a place's best keyword against a P75 of Segment-level demand. With a floor of 100 and a union over 6 markets, it could easily reach 50%, which means Tier Q of about 7.5 USD live.

Verdict: the design's 17 USD is arithmetically correct at live prices. A cost-first version should cost about 8–10 USD in all for the same coverage: standard queue, pruned DE/FR/NL, and a SERP for every place with volume, which drops the shortlist machinery.
flaws: Prices are taken from DFS live mode without looking at the standard queue. All three paid calls hit /live (dataforseo_client.py:254,300,350,454). For an offline admin batch, task_post plus tasks_ready is roughly 3x cheaper for SERP (about 0.0006 against 0.002) and about 1.5x cheaper for Google Ads volumes. That alone roughly halves the 15.2 USD DFS. The rates come from DFS public pricing and need checking with a one-task probe on the account.

The Tier Q shortlist costs more in complexity than it saves: about 6.3 USD one time against design A. In exchange it adds market_demand_bar, a V → recompute → bar → Q → recompute chain, a unit mismatch (place keyword volume against a Segment-level P75), and an unmeasured 25–40% share. At standard-queue prices, a SERP for every place with volume (about 4.5 USD) is cheaper than the live shortlist (5.0) and needs no bar or shortlist code.

The question_fill queue rebuilds a tenant → purchase path (the AA-646 lesson) to save cents. If every place with volume gets PAA in pass 1, the queue only matters for new places, and the monthly incremental run already covers those.

The 26.5 USD hard ceiling is not derived. The true worst case is 4 keywords per place (Tier V about 15.6) plus a shortlist equal to every place with volume (Tier Q about 15.1 at a 30% retry share): about 30.8 USD DFS, above the 27.41 balance. The 22 USD cap protects the balance, but a cap hit midway leaves Tier Q partial unless the runs are ordered strictly by tier.

The full 1,000-keyword task price is unverified, and the design treats it as flat. cost_guard.py:44-46 documents the price rising with keyword count (0.057 at 13 keywords or fewer, 0.09 at about 150). Nothing guards against a further step above 395. The design needs a probe task with an abort threshold before committing 113 tasks.

DE/FR/NL volumes are bought with language_code 'en' (seed_builder.py:53,61). That is about 5.13 USD for data the design itself calls understated. It pays full price for poor data instead of dropping the language filter or pruning Stage 2 to the keywords with volume in the Stage 1 markets.

Refresh cadence is costly for slow-moving place volumes. The 182-day full refresh (about 10.2 USD, 1.7/month amortised) re-buys keywords that returned 0 or null. Google Ads already returns 12 months of history (seasonality), so a 365-day refresh limited to keywords with volume would cost about 0.4–0.85 USD/month.

The LLM keyword map pays 1.85 USD to re-propose keywords for places whose keywords are already in search_demand. Seeding place_keyword_map from the existing rows is free and keeps continuity with the October data.

Each incremental run pays at least one volume task per market (0.54 USD for 6 markets) whatever the batch size. Monthly cadence for about 300 places pays that floor 12 times a year; quarterly batching, or a minimum batch size, would cut it to 4.

The cost model leaves out the Jev decide() calls and the Cohere embeddings triggered by the new recompute link on 31+ Segments × 6 markets. Calling the steady state '3–4 USD/month' is therefore a DFS+Haiku figure, not the full bill.

The four new tables, the contested-writer wiring and the per-market bar mix in product changes (Slate output changes) that are not needed to get the data. That widens the review surface of a risky migration PR (schema plus grants) for no cost benefit.
strengths: Keeps the one-buyer model (the admin/platform research job), and S1 and T2 never buy. That removes the 13–82 USD of DFS per S1 catalogue rerun, the largest avoidable cost in the audit.

Packs volumes into full 1,000-keyword tasks per market and keeps the 182-day cache skip. It gets the per-task unit economics right: about 1.7 USD per market against about 3.3 at today's 200-place runs.
Buys PAA once, US/English, and reads it in every market. That ends the 6x SERP-per-market multiplier, the biggest line in today's 80–95 USD design.
Persists the LLM keyword map, so Haiku is paid once per place rather than once per run per market.
The arithmetic is transparent and reproducible from the live facts. Unmeasured assumptions (shortlist share, retry share, the 1,000-keyword price, the C1 scope) are labelled honestly.
Staged approvals (US+UK+AU first, then DE/FR/NL) with a per-run USD cap in place of MAX_PLACES_PER_RUN. Both fit startup-scale cost discipline.
Covers every writer: S1, T2, T7, T8, T9, the quarter plan, and A3 ranking. The T2 relevant_keywords filter guards against the DFS_INTENT_UNDERUSED penalty.
Proxy markets (CA→US, NZ→AU, SG/HK/AE→UK) avoid paying for new markets until a paying tenant needs one.
The recompute link closes the gap where paid data never reached the Slate. The audit showed Blog-eligible Segments going from 4 to 31 after a recompute.
steal: Switch the research job to the DFS standard queue (task_post plus tasks_ready plus task_get, or a pingback) for both search_volume and SERP advanced. It is an offline batch, so latency does not matter. Check the account's standard rates with one probe task per endpoint first; expected saving is about 50% of DFS.

Drop the Tier Q shortlist and buy one US/en SERP (standard queue) for every place with any volume (about 5.7k places, about 4–5 USD with retries). That removes market_demand_bar as a research dependency, the two-pass order problem and most of the need for the tenant-fed question_fill queue.

Prune by market in sequence: Stage 2 (DE/FR/NL) buys only keywords with non-zero volume in any Stage 1 market. Request non-English markets without language_code (all languages; check the DFS docs) so place-name searches are counted. Expected cost about 0.7 USD per market instead of 1.71, with better data.

Probe-and-abort on the first volume task: send a full 1,000-keyword task first and stop the run if its billed cost is above about 0.10 USD. That proves the flat-price assumption before 113 tasks are committed.
Order the run strictly by tier under the cap: Tier V for every approved market completes before any Tier Q spend, so a cap hit never leaves volumes partial.
Seed place_keyword_map from the keywords already in search_demand at no cost. Pay Haiku only for places that have none.
Refresh volumes yearly and only for keywords that had volume. Google Ads monthly_searches already gives seasonality, which halves or better the 10.2 USD semiannual refresh.
Batch incremental research quarterly, or at a minimum of about 1,000 new keywords, so each run fills its per-market volume task instead of paying a 0.54 USD floor every month.
Keep the design's import-guard test (no DFS client in v1_*, T2, T7, T8, T9) and the per-run USD cap with a per-tier preview. They are cheap and enforce the one-buyer rule.

cost_check:
I recomputed the cost from the live facts, using 2.565 keywords per place and 0.09 USD per task of up to 1,000 keywords per market. The design's arithmetic is right. Its central figure, about 17.0 USD, is reasonable but rests on unmeasured inputs.

Tier V (volumes):
- US: 6,962 places × 2.565 = 17,858 keywords → 18 tasks → 1.62 USD.
- UK and AU: 7,145 × 2.565 = 18,327 → 19 tasks → 1.71 USD each.
- DE, FR and NL: 7,243 × 2.565 = 18,578 → 19 tasks → 1.71 USD each.
- Sum: 1.62 + 5 × 1.71 = 10.17 USD.
- Worst case at 4 keywords per place: US 28 tasks, the other five 29 each, so 173 tasks × 0.09 = 15.57 USD. The design says 15.7, which is fine.

LLM keyword map: 7,323 × 0.000253 = 1.85 USD.

Tier Q (questions):
- Places with volume: 7,323 × 0.773 = 5,661.
- Shortlist at 33%: 1,868 places. Cost = 1,868 × 0.002 + 0.3 × 1,868 × 0.00225 = 3.74 + 1.26 = 5.00 USD.

Totals:
- First pass: 10.17 + 5.00 + 1.85 = 17.02 USD (DFS 15.17).
- Stage 1 (US+UK+AU): 5.04 + 1.85 + 4.6 = 11.49 USD.
- Stage 2 (DE/FR/NL): 5.13 + 0.4 = 5.53 USD.
