Missing from the estimate, all small:
- Jev decide() calls during research and recompute.
- Cohere embeddings of about 10k new PAA questions (cents).
- The unexplained off-ledger drain (about 0.7–1.5 USD).

One concrete error: the proposed per-run DFS cap of 22 USD conflicts with the existing pre-check in segment_research_job.run. That check raises NonRetryable when the DFS balance is below the run's DFS budget. After Stage 1 (about 9.6 USD of DFS) the balance is about 17.8 USD. A Stage 2 job with a 22 USD cap therefore refuses to start. Caps must be set per stage, at or below the live balance (for example Stage 1 DFS 12, Stage 2 DFS 7).
flaws: S1 cannot use C9 for NEW tours. The pipeline runs A1→A3 (S1 rewrite → review/Master → atomize), so a new tour has no atom places when S1 runs. 'Title + atom places' then gives only a title match, so S1 writes new tours without keywords and never gets them back unless the tour is rewritten again. The design claims S1 is covered but never names this order dependency. It needs a fallback: places taken from the source text (as seed_builder does today), or a deliberate S1 'keywords on rerun only' rule.

Recompute coupling blocks deploys and DB Migrate. CIS has idle_exempt_kinds: [] (infra/AA-CIS-Infra/db/owners.yaml:120). A platform recompute has concurrency 1, expected_seconds 1800, and a debounce that can slide out to MAX_WAIT_S of 1,200 s. With question_fill draining 'within minutes' of tenant actions, and every drain enqueueing a recompute, tenant activity now keeps shared.job busy and blocks CIS backend deploys and DB Migrate apply (DM-11.4). The research run itself is a job of 1 hour or more over about 7k places × 6 markets, followed by two chained recomputes. For a 1–2 person team that releases daily, this gating will hurt.

'Limited to the affected Segments' is overstated. In recompute_job, segment_ids only limits the PAA re-landing. recompute_rankings_and_routes still re-ranks all 6 markets and re-detects routes every time. So each question_fill drain triggers a full platform ranking pass, not a cheap local update.

The chain V → recompute → bar → Q → recompute is an orchestration trap. On the first run market_demand_bar is empty. Tier Q therefore depends on a recompute finishing between two paid tiers, in two jobs that someone has to chain. If the operator forgets, or the recompute fails or is debounced, the shortlist is built from no bar or an old bar. The design admits the place-level vs Segment-level mismatch but leaves the chaining open.

The question_fill_request table plus a tenant-pool INSERT grant into acp_contract adds a new tenant write path into a CIS contract schema (a risky migration and grant), purely to signal need. question_topup already derives its needs from tenant Blog subjects by query (question_topup.py:55-66). A platform drain could derive slate questions_pending, picked routes and recent T2 tours by reading existing tables, with no new grant and no tenant-originated rows.

The failure mode from 25/09 is not designed out explicitly for Tier Q. place_question_log is written with questions_found, and a place with fewer than 3 questions is logged for 365 days. The design does not say that a DFS error, a payment failure, or a balance at zero must NOT write place_question_log. If it does, one bad run marks about 1,800 places 'done for a year' with no PAA, which is exactly the 25/09 corruption pattern moved to a new table.

Synchronous expiry cliff. All about 7k places are bought on one day, so every Tier V row goes stale on the same day 182 days later (about May 2027), and every Tier Q row on the same day a year later. Readers do not filter by age (grep: no interval or fetched_at filter on search_demand in the slate, atom_ranking, real_questions or s1_prefetch reads), so the data does not vanish. But the C11 guard will flip to 100% stale at once and demand one 10 USD approval. Expiry is not spread out, and zero-volume keywords (about 23%) are re-bought on every refresh.

Scope creep beyond DFS optimisation. Wiring the compute_contested writer changes Slate output and needs its own calibration. Proxy markets, a per-market relative bar, and a frontend coverage page plus a daily guard job are all bundled in. With 13 components, 4 new tables, a new job kind, a migration with grants, frontend work and a T2 validate change, the approved run is blocked behind weeks of work. The run actually needs only C1 + C3 + C10 + C7 + ledger tagging + a simple Tier Q shortlist.

Tier V for DE/FR/NL uses English keywords with language en, so it buys mostly null or near-zero volumes (5.13 USD). The relative bar then lets thin-market noise through (P75 of a few tens). The design accepts this, but it gives no cheap probe to check the non-null share first.

One job per stage is a big blast radius. A deploy, OOM or heartbeat failure part-way through a run of 7k places (max_attempts 2) is resumable only because the research and keyword-map logs skip done work. Nothing chunks or caps wall time, and the existing estimate (expected_seconds 3600) was set for 200 places.

LLM pricing assumes Haiku at 0.000253 USD per place. acc3 has been blocked since 29/10, so the interim gateway route is OpenAI or acc2 models. The per-place LLM cost and output quality on the route actually used are not verified, so the 1.85 USD figure belongs to whatever route the gateway resolves to.
strengths: One buyer and one store. S1 and T2 stop buying, and import-guard tests keep T2, T7, T8 and T9 DFS-free. This removes the 13–82 USD S1 rerun exposure and the AA-646 class of accidental spend.

Volume tasks are packed to full 1,000-keyword tasks, and PAA is bought once (US, English) and read market-agnostically. This is the right cost lever: Tier V is about 1.7 USD per market, and questions are no longer bought per market.
The persisted place_keyword_map makes the LLM a one-time cost per place instead of per run and per market.
The recompute link (C7) closes the real gap the audit found: purchases never reached the Slate. The Blog-eligible count went from 4 to 31 once research and recompute both ran.

Readers become plural and honest. Per-market demand rows fix the bug where the lowest-rank 'best market' let DE/FR/NL hide US/UK volume. demand None is treated as no_data, not 0, and the visible reason codes (no_data / below_bar / questions_pending) make coverage gaps diagnosable.
Staged approvals (US+UK+AU first, then measure, then DE/FR/NL) fit the 27.41 USD balance. The arithmetic is transparent and reproducible, and the upper-bound caveats are stated honestly.
The coverage guard (C11) and ledger tagging (C12) give a 1–2 person team a daily signal instead of relying on memory.
Google Ads Keyword Planner is evaluated correctly: no PAA, bucketed volumes on low-spend accounts, and a developer token plus OAuth to set up. It is deferred, which is the right call.
steal: Per-stage DFS caps at or below the live balance (for example Stage 1 DFS 12, Stage 2 DFS 7), so the existing balance pre-check in segment_research_job does not refuse Stage 2. Also add a daily balance-vs-ledger reconciliation to the guard, so the off-ledger spender is caught by the balance, not the ledger.

Drop the tenant-written queue table. The platform drain derives its needs by query from existing state (Slate questions_pending reasons, picked Blog Routes, T2 jobs in the last N days), the same way question_topup does today. This means no tenant-pool grant into acp_contract and no tenant-originated rows.

Drain on a schedule (one nightly batch), not 'within minutes'. That gives one debounced recompute per night, keeps shared.job idle during working hours for deploys and DB Migrate, and T9 still benefits because PlacePaaSource reads search_demand directly without a recompute.

Remove the V → recompute → Q dependency. Build the Tier Q shortlist from a place-level rule computed inside the research job, for example 'best keyword volume ≥ 100 in any market' or the top-N places by best volume. Then one job runs V then Q, and one recompute follows at the end. The per-market Segment bar stays a Slate-only concern.

Never write place_question_log or segment_research_log on a DFS error, a payment failure or a zero balance. Only a successful response, even an empty one, counts as 'researched'. Add a unit test that injects a 402 or payment failure and checks that nothing is logged.

Spread expiry: give each refresh a random offset of ±30 days, or refresh 1/6 of the catalogue each month under the standing monthly cap. Give zero-volume keywords a 365-day TTL so they are not re-bought every 182 days.
Chunk the research into resumable jobs of about 1,000 places, each under the stage cap. Run them outside working hours so job-idle windows for deploys stay predictable.

S1 fallback for new tours: when a tour has no atoms yet, derive places from the source text through the existing seed_builder and read search_demand by those place names. If nothing matches, write keyword-free and let the next rerun pick keywords up. State this rule explicitly.
Probe before Stage 2: one volume task each for DE, FR and NL on a sample of about 300 places (0.27 USD) to measure the non-null share of English keywords, before spending 5.13 USD on the full pass.

Ship the minimal run-enabling slice first: C1 scope filter, full-task volumes, the USD gate, a simple Tier Q shortlist, the recompute link and ledger tagging. Ship the reader changes for T2, T7, T8 and S1 (C8, C9, the per-market bar) as a second PR wave. Split the contested writer out into its own issue.

cost_check:
The arithmetic is right for the inputs it chose, but some of those inputs are optimistic. The design also leaves out the biggest unit-price lever.

1) Recomputing exactly as the design does (k = 395/154 = 2.565 keywords per place, 0.09 USD per volume task, 0.002 USD per SERP, s = 77.3%, LLM 0.000253 USD per place):
- Volumes: US 6,962 × 2.565 = 17,858 → 18 tasks = 1.62. UK/AU 7,145 → 18,327 → 19 tasks = 1.71 each. DE/FR/NL 7,243 → 18,578 → 19 tasks = 1.71 each. Total 10.17.
- LLM: 7,323 × 0.000253 = 1.85.
- SERP: 6,962 × 0.773 × 0.002 = 10.76.
- Phase 1 = 5.04 + 1.85 + 10.76 = 17.65. Phase 2 = 5.13. Total 22.78. Matches the design's ≈22.8 / 17.7 / 5.1.

2) Where the number is too low:
(a) k is measured AFTER the cache. `_buy_volumes` (segment_research_batch.py:263-307) skips keywords already fresh in search_demand. The 154 "old" places almost certainly had cache hits from 25/09 data, so 2.565 is a net figure. The code's own estimate constant is KEYWORDS_PER_PLACE = 4. At k = 4, volumes become US 28 tasks (2.52) and the other five markets 29 tasks each (2.61): 15.57 for 6 markets, 7.74 for Phase 1.
(b) The SERP base uses the US volume-stale count (6,962). The design's own trigger is different: PAA freshness is a new column (paa_retrieved_on, so effectively every place is due), and the SERP buys for volume > 0 in ANY market. The correct base is 7,323 × s_any, with s_any ≥ 0.773. That gives 11.3 to about 12.5 at s_any ≈ 0.85.
(c) The "ceiling" of 35.07 is not a ceiling, because it uses the measured k. A real ceiling (k = 4, LLM at its ceiling, SERP for every place) is 15.57 + 10.25 + 14.65 = 40.5 USD, before Jev.
(d) Jev/TypeSafe decide() runs once per proposed keyword (`_gate_keywords`, segment_research_batch.py:212-235). That is about 7,323 × ~3 ≈ 20,000+ decisions on the first pass, and none of it is in the estimate. It can be measured for free from llm_call_log (provider typesafe) for the 08/11 job 287e1c14. Measure it before approval: at even 0.001 USD per decision it costs about as much as the whole SERP tier.

Realistic band, my calculation, DFS only:
- Phase 1 (US+UK+AU): 17.7–22.1 USD.
- All 6 markets: 22.8–30 USD.
- Then the off-ledger DFS drop of 0.7–1.5 USD on top.
- After Phase 1 the balance is about 3.8–9 USD, so at the upper end Phase 2 does not fit without a top-up.

3) The missed lever: every call goes to the /live endpoints (dataforseo_client.py:254, 300, 350, 454). Research is an approved, non-urgent batch, so it could use DFS Standard queue (task_post → tasks_ready → task_get). As far as I know DFS's public price list (not checked today — confirm on the pricing page or with one billed task) has Standard at about 0.0006 per SERP against 0.002 live (−70%), and Google Ads search_volume at about 0.05 per task against ~0.075 live (−33%). Applying those ratios to the measured rates:
- SERP: 7,323 × 0.773 × 0.0006 ≈ 3.4.
- Volumes: about 5.7–6.8.
- LLM: 1.85.
- All 6 markets ≈ 11–12 USD instead of 22.8. Phase 1 ≈ 8–9.

4) Value per dollar of Phase 2: `resolve_buyer_markets` passes language 'en' by default (seed_builder.py:404, 437), and the proposals are English. So DE/FR/NL buy English-keyword volumes in Germany, France and the Netherlands, which will be mostly null or tiny. The 5.13 USD now, plus about 5.1 at every refresh, mostly buys proof of zeros. Because the Slate takes the MAX only over a tenant's OWN markets, a DE-only agency still won't clear the 1,000 bar.

5) "Today's design ≈ 80–95" is a straw man. One run of today's code with all 6 markets already pays the LLM once (not 6 × 1.85), and suggestions can already be turned off. In DE/FR/NL with 'en', few keywords have volume > 0, so per-market SERPs there are fewer. A realistic figure for today's code is about 40–55. The real saving is "SERP once per place", which is still a solid 2× or more.

6) Monthly ≈ 1.1 USD is correct arithmetic (6 minimum tasks 0.54 + SERP 0.46 + LLM 0.08). But it rests on an unvalidated assumption of 300 new places a month. The keyword map is keyed by the canonical_place string, so re-atomize renames re-pay the LLM and Jev (volumes and SERP are reused only if the new proposals land on the same keywords). The amortised 3.7 USD/month assumes a 182-day volume refresh that is not needed for 12-month-average data.
flaws: The cost model ignores DFS Standard-queue pricing. Every research call hits the /live endpoints, yet research is admin-approved batch work with no latency need. Standard queue would cut the SERP tier by about 70% and volumes by about 33%, roughly halving the first pass (≈22.8 → ≈11–12 USD for 6 markets). This is the single biggest unit-price lever and it is missing.

Jev/TypeSafe decide() runs once per proposed keyword (_gate_keywords), about 20,000+ calls on a full first pass, and is left out as 'unmeasured'. It can be measured for free from llm_call_log for job 287e1c14 and could rival the SERP tier. The design asks for approval without it.

k = 2.565 keywords per place is a post-cache figure, because _buy_volumes skips keywords fresh in search_demand and the 154-place sample was pre-researched. A full-catalogue gross k may be close to the code's own KEYWORDS_PER_PLACE = 4, which adds about 2.7 USD to Phase 1 and 5.4 USD to all 6 markets.

The SERP base is the US volume-stale count (6,962), but the design's own rule (PAA freshness is a new column; volume > 0 in ANY market) puts all 7,323 places due, at a higher share than 77.3%. That is about 11.3–12.5 USD, not 10.76.

The 35.07 'ceiling' uses measured rates and is not an upper bound. The true ceiling is about 40.5 USD plus Jev. With the off-ledger drop, the 27.41 balance may not cover Phase 1 plus Phase 2 at the upper end.

Phase 2 (DE/FR/NL, 5.13 USD now plus about 5.1 per refresh) buys volumes for ENGLISH keywords with language_code 'en' in non-English markets, so the data is mostly null or tiny. Because the Slate takes the MAX only over a tenant's own markets, DE/FR/NL-only agencies still won't clear the 1,000 bar. Poor value per dollar until keywords are localised.

The 'today's design ≈80–95' comparison is inflated: a single multi-market run already pays the LLM once and can disable suggestions. A realistic figure is about 40–55, so the claimed saving is overstated by about 2×.
'Recovers ~16.65 USD of October purchases' is rhetoric. The backfill does not lower any phase cost in the estimate, and the S1 keyword ideas are tour-level terms whose mapping to places is heuristic.

The 182-day volume refresh (about 10 USD each time) is unnecessary for 12-month-average Google Ads data. Annual refresh, or refreshing only keywords near a bar, would halve that line. Zero-volume keywords are re-bought at every refresh.

The keyword map is keyed by the canonical_place string, so re-atomize renames (cause of the 7,116 stale places unknown) re-pay the LLM and Jev. Monthly cost depends on rename churn, not the assumed 300 new places. There is no plan to carry the map over through segment aliases.

S1 loses its tour-level head terms (keywords_for_keywords ideas such as country + theme + duration). The place-level map will not produce them, so S1 meta quality may drop with no cost line to restore them.

Complexity relative to the DFS saving: the saving comes almost entirely from SERP once per place, suggestions off, a persisted map and S1 not buying. The tour_seo_pack table, its fingerprints, a rebuild job, a nightly sweep and a PK change on segment_research_log add migration and operations risk and save no DFS. A shared loader function (approach A) gets the same cost.
The '≥100 SERP gate ≈ half' saving is an unmeasured guess presented as ≈17.4 USD.
strengths: Correctly finds that SERP per market is the main cost driver, and buys PAA, related searches and domains once per place at US/en, which is what every consumer (English-only) actually uses.
Uses full 1,000-keyword volume tasks per market, so volumes become a minor line (about 1.6–1.7 USD per market per pass).
A persisted place→keyword map means the LLM (and potentially Jev) is paid once per place across markets and refreshes.
S1 stops buying per tour (removing a 13–82 USD per full rerun exposure), and one buyer with a USD gate, a balance pre-check and a monthly cap matches the 'active purchase only' principle.
keywords_for_keywords is off by default and allowed only as full 20-seed tasks, which stops the proven waste of tasks with few obscure seeds.
Tiered freshness (volumes vs PAA) and a research → recompute link mean purchased data actually reaches the Slate. That was the real gap behind the 4 → 31 Blog-eligible jump.
Phased approval (US+UK+AU first) and a check of the first 1,000-keyword task in dfs_call_log are sensible cost controls.
The proxy map (CA→US, NZ→AU, SG/HK/AE→UK) avoids paying for new markets while no longer dropping tenants silently.
steal: Run research through DFS Standard queue (task_post / tasks_ready / task_get) instead of /live for the volume and SERP tiers. Verify the price with one billed task first. Expected to roughly halve the first pass and every refresh.

Before approval, read the Jev/TypeSafe cost for job 287e1c14 from llm_call_log (provider typesafe) and include a measured per-place Jev rate. Persist Jev verdicts in place_keyword_map so they are never paid again.
Measure gross k (keywords_cached + keywords_bought) from the 08/11 job stats and use it in the estimate instead of net k.

Fill partial tasks for free. The last task in each market has spare slots (US 142, UK/AU ~673). Pad them with tour-level head terms (country + theme + duration from tour titles), which gives S1 its head keywords back at zero marginal cost.

Defer Phase 2: treat DE/FR/NL as proxied to UK until localised keywords exist (language de/fr/nl plus translated proposals), and buy them only when such a tenant actually writes in that language. Saves 5.13 USD now and about 5 USD per refresh.
Refresh volumes yearly, not every 182 days, and in a refresh only re-buy keywords with volume > 0 or within a band around the bars (e.g. 300–3,000). Re-check all-zero keywords every 2 years.
Carry place_keyword_map entries across canonical_place renames using the existing segment alias writes, so re-atomize churn does not re-pay LLM and Jev.
Order SERP purchases by consumer value (places in tenant tours and Segments near the Blog bar first) so a balance-limited run buys the useful PAA first.
Show the balance after Phase 1 at the upper bound (≈3.8 USD) in the /plan preview and require a top-up decision before Phase 2.

cost_check:
The arithmetic is correct for the inputs the design chose, but the inputs lean low.

- Tier V: ceil(6,962×2.565/1000)=18 tasks → 1.62 (US). UK/AU 19 → 1.71 each. DE/FR/NL 19 → 1.71 each. Sum 10.17 is right.
- LLM: 7,323×0.000253 = 1.85, right.
- Tier Q central: 7,323×0.773 = 5,661 places with volume. ×0.33 = 1,868. 1,868×0.002 = 3.74, plus 30% depth-2 retries 1,868×0.3×0.00225 = 1.26, so 5.00. Range 3.79–6.06 is right.
- First pass: DFS 15.17 + LLM 1.85 ≈ 17.0. Stage 1: 5.04 + 1.85 + 4.6 = 11.5. Stage 2: 5.13 + 0.4 = 5.5. Both right.

Where the number is weak:
1. The "hard ceiling ≈ 26.5" cannot be rebuilt from the components. Worst case is V 15.66 + Q 6.06 + LLM 1.85 = 23.6. With the old LLM ceiling of 10.25 it is ≈ 32. 26.5 is really the proposed caps (DFS 22 + LLM 4), so label it that way.
2. 2.565 keywords per place and the 77.3% volume share both come from 154 places in one tenant's tours. Those tours lean to popular places, and part of the 395 bought keywords may have been net of fresh cache hits. Haiku is asked for up to 4 keywords per place. So Tier V is more likely 12–15.7 than 10.2.
3. The Tier Q shortlist share depends on a Blog bar that has not been chosen. With a 100 floor in the US (proposed), the shortlist could be 50%+ of places with volume, which puts Tier Q at ≈ 7.5–9.
4. My realistic first pass: DFS 15–22 + LLM 1.9 ≈ 17–24 USD, still inside the 27.41 balance but with less headroom than the ~12 claimed.
5. Not costed and possibly material: Jev decide() calls, which are prepaid Jev credit. That is about 18.8k a3_keyword_belongs pairs (7,323×2.565) at research, plus up to 3 a3_demand_belongs calls per Segment across 11,594 Segments at recompute. Also Cohere embeddings of the new PAA. This bill scales with keyword count, not task count.
6. Design A gives one SERP to every place with volume: 10.17 + 11.32 + 1.85 = 23.3, as stated. C saves only about 6 USD over A one-off, and about 3 USD/yr on PAA refresh.
7. Monthly 0.9–1.8 is consistent if churn is about 300 new places a month. That churn is assumed, not measured.
flaws: S1 gap for NEW tours. The pipeline runs S1 rewrite, then review/Master, then A3 atomize. A brand-new tour has no v_active_tour_atoms places and no researched keywords when S1 runs. Research is a monthly batch after re-atomize. So C9 build_seo_context_from_demand gives new tours only title-place matches, usually nothing, and S1 writes them keyword-less forever unless the SEO meta is regenerated after research. The design keeps the S1_SEO_BUY path only as an emergency switch and has no 'regenerate meta after research' step.

T2 first-rewrite PAA gap. Tier Q covers only shortlisted places (~33%). The t2_tour queue rows only help the NEXT rewrite, and tenants usually rewrite a tour once. The drain also ships with QUESTION_FILL_ENABLED=false. So on day one, T2 PAA (and T9 Route FAQ via route_pick) is limited to shortlisted places until a second approval. T2 PAA coverage per tenant market is therefore weaker than design A.

T2 for non-English tenants is not handled. t2_rewrite_job carries rewrite_language, and DE/FR/NL agencies (9 declarations) may rewrite in German, French or Dutch. Tier V buys English keywords with language 'en' in those markets: demand is undercounted and in the wrong language for the output. relevant_keywords checks coverage against the English source, so English phrases could be pushed into German meta. DFS_INTENT_UNDERUSED (graph.py:1215-1236) is report-only only for v2 drafts; T2 on the legacy path still takes the -1.0. The design needs 'no DFS keywords when rewrite_language is not EN' (or translated keywords), not just a 3-tour check.

S1 and T2 lose tour-intent keywords. handler.fetch_all seeds from the tour name, activities and extra seeds, plus SERP related searches and keywords_for_keywords long-tail. The store holds only ≤4 Haiku place keywords per place. For tour pages this replaces '<activity> <region>'-style tour intent with place-name intent. The quality impact is unmeasured; only T9 gets a 3-blog check, S1 gets none.

Tier Q is chained to a product decision that has not been made. The shortlist reads market_demand_bar, which needs a recompute after Tier V, and the bar floor/percentile is still open. Pass 1 therefore cannot run as one job: V, recompute, bar, Q, recompute. Changing the bar later changes who gets PAA after the money is spent. A fixed purchase threshold (volume ≥ N in any market) would decouple buying from the Slate bar.

Too much machinery for about 6 USD. C adds 4 new tables (place_keyword_map, place_question_log, question_fill_request, market_demand_bar), a new job kind, a tenant INSERT grant, a kill switch, proxy labels and a contested-writer flag. Against design A that saves ~6 USD one-off. The queue also brings back a tenant-action-to-spend link (the AA-646 lesson), capped at 1 USD/month but still a new attack and bug surface.

The cost inputs are biased low (one tenant's 154 popular places, cache-netted keyword count). Jev decide and Cohere costs, which scale with ~18.8k keyword pairs and ~11.6k Segments, are left out. They could be the same order as the DFS volume cost.

US-only PAA is stored under US rows. atom_ranking.precompute_question_landings reads only rows with search_volume IS NOT NULL. The fix to include US-PAA2 rows is listed, but if it ships out of order, the depth-2 top-up answers stay invisible to the ranking questions axis and the Blog bar.
Contested writer: wiring it is scope creep inside a cost redesign. It changes Slate output and needs calibration, and it is not needed for any writer to get its data.
C1 scope filter is unmeasured, so every figure is an upper bound. The real numbers could be quite a bit lower, which also weakens the case for the costly-to-build Tier Q shortlist.
strengths: One buyer, one store. S1 stops buying, which removes the 13–82 USD per catalogue rerun, the largest recurring DFS risk after 25/09.
Tier V packs keywords into full 1,000-keyword tasks across all 6 markets at about 1.7 USD each. That gives T2 real per-market volumes and puts demand on far more ranking rows.
PAA as market-agnostic English is a sound saving: no per-market SERP fan-out. PlacePaaSource already reads any market.
Persisted place_keyword_map: the LLM is paid once per place for its lifetime, Jev verdicts are reused, and refreshes need no LLM.
Fixes the real coverage bug: research enqueues a debounced recompute (C7). Today paid data does not reach the Slate without an unrelated recompute.
T7 per-market rows replace the lowest-total_rank 'best market' pick, and no_data / below_bar / questions_pending reasons are added. This answers AA-1055 directly.
T2 goes plural over tenant markets with a MAX volume, plus the relevant_keywords filter, keeping the T2 no-DFS test.
A labelled proxy map for unsupported tenant markets (CA→US, NZ→AU, SG/HK/AE→UK). Real markets are bought only for paying tenants.
Ledger attribution (tenant_id/job_id/tier) and an import-guard test against DFS in tenant paths.
A two-stage approval (US+UK+AU, then DE/FR/NL) that fits the 27.41 balance.
steal: Replace the bar-driven Tier Q shortlist with a fixed purchase threshold, e.g. best volume ≥ 50–100 in any market, as the AA-1055 comment proposed. No V→recompute→bar→Q chain, no dependence on the open Blog-bar decision. At ~50–60% of places with volume it costs ~6–8 USD, still far below today's design.

Or simply buy one US/en SERP for every place with volume in pass 1 (design A, ~11.3 USD of SERP). Then drop or defer the question_fill_request queue, its tenant INSERT grant and the kill switch. T2 first rewrites, S1 and T9 Route FAQs are covered immediately for ~6 USD more.

Add a free post-research SEO-meta refresh for tours written before their places were researched (new tours in the S1→atomize order). Rebuild seo_context from demand and regenerate only seo_title/meta, with no DFS.
T2 rule: when rewrite_language is not EN, pass no DFS keywords (or only place-name keywords that stay unchanged across languages) and keep DFS_INTENT_UNDERUSED report-only for T2.
Refresh volumes yearly, not every 182 days. Google Ads search_volume is a 12-month average, so this saves about 10 USD/yr with little quality loss.

Measure before pricing: run a free preview on the C1-filtered scope and log the Haiku proposals per place on a 200-place sample (no DFS). Re-derive keywords/place and the volume share outside the audit tenant before asking for approval.
Cost Jev decide calls and Cohere embeddings in the preview (count of keyword pairs × Jev rate, segments × tries) next to DFS and LLM.
Keep Tier I off and keep C12 ledger plus import-guard tests exactly as proposed.

cost_check:
I recomputed the cost from the live facts: k=2.565 keywords per place, 77.3% of places get a SERP, 0.09 USD per volume task of up to 1,000 keywords, 0.002 USD per SERP, 0.000253 USD of LLM per place.

VOLUMES: 10.17. The arithmetic checks out: US ceil(17,858/1000)=18 tasks = 1.62, then 5 markets × 19 tasks = 8.55. The input k=2.565 is soft, though. It was measured after the fresh-keyword cache dedupe in _buy_volumes, and KEYWORDS_PER_PLACE allows up to 4. With k=4 it is 30 tasks × 6 markets = 16.2.

LLM keyword map: 1.85 (Haiku only). Jev a3_keyword decide() calls on about 18–29k keywords are not counted.

SERP: undercounted. paa_retrieved_on is a NEW column, so it is NULL for every row and the 365-day skip saves nothing on the first pass. The base is therefore all 7,323 in-scope places, not the 6,962 stale US places. The share is also volume>0 in ANY market, which is at least 77.3%. That gives 7,323 × 0.77–0.85 × 0.002 = 11.3–12.4, against the design's 10.76.

Realistic first pass: about 23.3–24.5 USD. The design says 22.8. With k=4 it rises to about 30, still under the 35 ceiling.
- Phase 1 (US+UK+AU): 5.04 + 1.85 + about 11.3 = about 18.2 (design 17.7).
- Phase 2 (DE/FR/NL volumes): 5.13.
- Balance after both phases: 27.41 − 23.3 = about 4.1. The off-ledger drain (about 0.7–1.5) and Jev bring it closer to 3. Tight, but it works.

BLOCKER the design omits: Phase 1 is about 16.3 USD of DFS in one run. That is above the dfs global cap of 10 USD/day and the job:segment_research cap of 5 USD/run (SAFE_DEFAULTS in shared/cost_guard.py:37-41; the live spend_budget values have not been read). The run would abort partway unless the budget rows are raised by an approved change, or the phase is split over at least 2 days and runs.

The 'today's design ≈80–95' comparison is inflated. Today's batch path already proposes LLM keywords ONCE per run across every market passed (research_batch takes all markets together). Its _buy_serps also buys a SERP only for markets where that keyword has volume>0 (with_volume), not for all 6. Today's code with the 6 markets in one run and use_suggestions=false comes to about 1.85 + 10.2 + SERP (US about 11, UK/AU about 9–11 each, DE/FR/NL lower because English-keyword volume is thinner there, about 5–7 each) ≈ 55–65 USD. Adding suggestions takes it to about 63–72. The real saving of B is about 30–40 USD. Nearly all of it comes from the 'one SERP per place at US/en' rule, which is a small change in _buy_serps/_serp_tool and needs no packs.

Monthly figures check out: 0.54 + 0.46 + 0.08 ≈ 1.1 per incremental run, 10.2 every 182 days and 10.8 every 365 days, ≈3.7/month amortised. The 300 new places a month is an assumption. Refreshing volumes yearly instead of every 182 days would cut the amortised figure to about 2.8/month: they are 12-month averages, and the design itself argues they barely move.
flaws: S1 and T2 lose tour-level keywords. S1's per-tour keywords_for_keywords is seeded with idea_seeds() (seed_builder.py:217-242): the tour-name seed, title places + country, and '{country} {activity}' ('bhutan trekking'). Those head terms are what seo_title/meta are written around. The place-level store only holds Haiku place phrases ('tiger's nest hike'). place_keyword_map is keyed by canonical_place, so a country+activity keyword cannot even be stored there. The Phase-0 backfill keeps such keywords only for tours S1 already fetched, US only, and only when they map to a place. New tours, and every non-US market, get none, because Tier I is off and seeds per place only. This is a real regression for S1 and T2 meta, and the design does not mention it.

The T2 penalty claim is wrong. graph.py:1215-1236 subtracts 1.0 whenever the keyword list is non-empty and NONE of them appears in seo_title/meta (it is report-only for S1 v2 drafts, never for T2). The relevant_keywords filter makes a match possible, not guaranteed. Filling packs for more tours still raises how often the penalty fires. The safe fix is to make DFS_INTENT_UNDERUSED report-only for T2 too, or to penalise only when a covered keyword existed and the writer ignored it.

T2 per tenant market ignores language. T2 has rewrite_language (t2_rewrite_job.py:644), and research buys DE/FR/NL volumes with language 'en' (the admin router passes {'countries': markets}, so language defaults to 'en'). A German- or French-writing tenant gets English keywords ranked by English-in-Germany volume. Its non-English meta can never contain them, so the −1.0 fires on every rewrite. T2 should pass keywords only when the rewrite language matches the keyword language.

The comparison baseline is a strawman (80–95). Today's code already proposes LLM keywords once per multi-market run and buys a SERP only in markets with volume. A fair baseline is about 55–72. The design's headline saving is overstated by about 2×.

Phase 1 does not fit the spend caps. About 16.3 USD of DFS in one run is above the 10 USD/day global and 5 USD/run segment_research caps (SAFE_DEFAULTS; live rows not read). The design replaces MAX_PLACES_PER_RUN with max_usd but never mentions raising or splitting the spend_budget rows. The run would abort partway and leave failed places.

The SERP estimate uses the US stale count (6,962). paa_retrieved_on is a new NULL column, so every in-scope place (7,323) qualifies, at an any-market volume share of at least 77%. That is 0.6–1.6 USD more than stated. Phase 1 lands at about 18.2.

The tour_seo_pack table is over-built for this scale (892 tours). It brings a table, a debounced job, a nightly fingerprint sweep, read-through rebuild on a mismatch, and a seo_context compatibility dual-write. Checking a fingerprint at read time already needs the tour's atom places plus the max retrieved_on of its rows, which is most of the work of building the pack. packs_for_tenant then merges markets at read time anyway. A pure function load_seo_pack(conn, tour_id, markets) over place_keyword_map + search_demand gives every writer the same object with no table, no job and no staleness class. Snapshot it into job.result or the T8 dfs_paa_snapshot for reproducibility (the WM-20 replay).

There are now two demand truths. Writers would join on exact keywords via place_keyword_map, while atom_ranking._demand() still claims keywords by name/word overlap. The pack and the Segment can disagree on a place's demand, and the Slate bar (ranking grain) and the T8/T9 block (pack grain) can tell different stories for the same piece. The design accepts this and only documents it.

S1 behaviour change hidden in the wave flow. A tour whose places are not researched is written keyword-less unless someone runs a scoped research pass first. The design relies on a runbook step, not a guard. s1_batch should refuse to start, or warn loudly, when the share of thin packs is above X.

The PAA rule has edge cases. A SERP 'for the best keyword with volume>0 in ANY market' at US/en can pick a keyword whose volume exists only in DE/NL, and the US SERP may then return no PAA. Places with zero volume everywhere (about 23%) get no PAA at all, so T9 place_paa and the A3 questions axis stay empty for them. The design does not quantify this gap or say whether the 31-of-176 Blog figure assumed PAA on these places.
The proxy map (SG/HK/AE→UK, CA→US, NZ→AU) is a product claim (UK demand stands in for Singapore) surfaced to tenants. It needs a sign-off as a product decision, not just a constant in seed_builder.

Unmeasured costs are hidden behind 'not included'. Jev decide() is called per proposed keyword (about 18–29k a3_keyword calls) plus the a3_demand_belongs calls at recompute. Jev is a paid provider, and that could be a material share of the LLM line. A trial (about 3 tours or 50 places) should measure Jev spend from llm_call_log before Phase 1.

The migration changes the segment_research_log PK to (place, market, tier). Existing rows need a tier backfill (volume, plus paa where PAA exists). The design does not specify it, and without it every place reads as PAA-due.
strengths: It is the only design so far that wires every writer to the per-place × market purchase store. T8 and T9 get demand for tours S1 never fetched, and T2 gets its tenant's markets plural instead of the singular tenant_market_seo with a US fallback.
Buying a SERP once per place at US/en is correct and is the single biggest saving. Every PAA consumer is English-only today: T9's looks_english filter, and the A3 questions pool.
The research → enqueue_recompute(platform, segment_ids, debounce) link closes the real gap from the audit (4 → 31 Blog-eligible only appeared after a manual recompute).
The Slate MAX-across-markets fix and the no_demand_data / below_bar / few_questions split directly address both a real bug (a thin market winning on median-imputed rank) and AA-1055's 'done when'.

place_keyword_map with prompt_version means the LLM is paid once per place across markets and refreshes. Freshness tracked per tier (volume 182 days, PAA 365 days) avoids buying PAA again on every volume refresh.
It sequences the T2 keyword_fit change before the purchase, extends the DFS import-guard test, and checks the price of the first 1,000-keyword task in dfs_call_log, aborting above 0.09.
The free Phase-0 backfill of the October S1 seo_context data into search_demand reuses data already paid for.
Its cost honesty is mostly good: rates are measured, caveats are listed, and the plan is phased so each step fits inside the balance.
S1 stops buying DFS per tour. A full catalogue rerun no longer has a 13–82 USD tail.
steal: One SERP per place at US/en, picking the best keyword with volume in any market, skipped when PAA is fresh. Implement it as a small change in _buy_serps/_serp_tool; it is most of the saving.

place_keyword_map (persisted LLM proposals with prompt_version, exact join), extended with a non-place key (country+activity / tour-level). Then '{country} {activity}' and title-place seeds can be bought as volume-only keywords, about 892 tours × 2 seeds ≈ 1,800 keywords ≈ 2 tasks per market ≈ 1 USD for 6 markets, instead of per-tour keywords_for_keywords. S1 and T2 keep head terms with no per-tour buying.
Research completion enqueues a debounced platform recompute scoped to the researched Segments.
Slate Blog bar = MAX demand across the tenant's markets, with the source market recorded, plus a no-data / below-bar / few-questions reason.

A shared keyword_fit.relevant_keywords for S1 v2 and T2. Also make DFS_INTENT_UNDERUSED report-only for T2, or fire it only when a covered keyword was ignored. And pass keywords to T2 only when rewrite_language matches the keyword language.
Freshness per tier in segment_research_log (volume vs PAA), with a v_research_due view as the work queue and a daily read-only stale-share guard (AA-1055).

A pure loader load_seo_pack(conn, tour_id, markets) shared by S1, T2, T8, T9 and quarter-plan, with a coverage status (ok/thin/empty) in job.result. Drop the materialised tour_seo_pack table, its job and the nightly sweep.
A free Phase-0 backfill of seo_context ideas and PAA into search_demand.
Proxy markets for CA/NZ/SG/HK/AE, labelled to staff and tenants, after a product sign-off.

Phase gating: a trial of about 50 places that measures real k, the SERP share and the Jev spend first. Raise or split the spend_budget rows explicitly (Phase 1 is above 10 USD/day). Check the price of the first full 1,000-keyword task and abort above 0.09.
Consider refreshing volumes every 365 days instead of 182. They are 12-month averages, and this saves about 10 USD a year.

cost_check:
The expected-case arithmetic is right. Using k=2.565 keywords/place, 0.09 USD per task of up to 1,000 keywords, SERP 0.002, s=77.3% and LLM 0.000253 USD/place:
- Volumes: US ceil(17,858/1000)=18 tasks = 1.62; UK/AU/DE/FR/NL 19 tasks each = 1.71 x 5 = 8.55. Total 10.17.
- LLM map: 7,323 x 0.000253 = 1.85.
- SERP once at US/en: 6,962 x 0.773 x 0.002 = 10.76.
- First pass: 22.78. Phase 1 (US+UK+AU): 5.04 + 1.85 + 10.76 = 17.65. Phase 2: 5.13.

Five things in the design's numbers are wrong or optimistic:
(1) The "ceiling ≈35.07" is not a ceiling. It reuses the measured k for volumes. With KEYWORDS_PER_PLACE=4 the volume ceiling is US 28 tasks (2.52) + 5 x 29 tasks (2.61 each) = 15.57. True ceiling = 15.57 + LLM 10.25 + SERP on all in-scope places 14.65 ≈ 40.5 USD. The DFS-only ceiling for Phase 1+2 is 30.2, above the 27.41 balance. The USD gate must be set below the balance, and a run can stop at the gate partway through. That is acceptable only because purchases already made stay cached.
(2) The "leaves ≈9.8 / ≈4.6 of 27.41" figures subtract the 1.85 USD of Haiku from the DFS balance. The LLM is billed through the AI gateway, not DFS. The DFS balance after Phase 1 is 27.41 − 15.80 = 11.61, and after Phase 2 it is 6.48. Then subtract the unexplained off-ledger drain of about 0.7–1.5 USD per fortnight.
(3) The SERP rule "best keyword with volume >0 in ANY market" makes s ≥ 77.3%, not equal to it, because 77.3% was measured on US only. In Phase 1, places with volume only in DE/FR/NL get no SERP. So Phase 2 is not purely volumes: either it buys a few SERPs or those places stay without PAA.
(4) The backfill does not "recover 16.65 USD". The S1 keyword ideas and PAA belong to tour seed keywords, not places. Mapping them to places needs the word-overlap/ILIKE heuristic the design says it removes, and the cost figures do not count the backfill as reducing Phase 1. It helps writers, not the bill.
(5) Two LLM costs are left out. The first post-run platform recompute calls Jev decide() per (segment, candidate keyword) (a3_demand_belongs, atom_ranking.py:242-263) over 11,594 Segments, and Cohere embeds the newly landed PAA. Research itself calls the Jev a3_keyword gate on ~18–29k keywords. None of these is in the 22.8 or the 35, and with denser data they scale up.

Honest summary: expected ≈22.8 USD all-in (≈20.9 DFS + 1.85 LLM + unmeasured Jev/Cohere), worst case ≈40 USD. Monthly incremental ≈1.0 DFS + 0.08 LLM, as stated, but only if renames from a re-atomize wave stay near 300 places a month. That assumption has not been measured.
flaws: The pack table is a cache whose check costs as much as rebuilding it. The fingerprint includes the max retrieved_on / paa_retrieved_on of the rows used, so checking freshness means running the same atom-places to keyword-map to search_demand join that builds the pack. Every read-through check, and the nightly sweep over 5,352 rows, does that join. With read-through in place, triggers (a)-(d) are only optimisations, yet each one is another failure path. Approach A (one shared loader function, no table) has the same correctness with fewer moving parts.

Read-through upsert from tenant paths. T2, T8 and T9 run in tenant job context and would write a platform table (acp_contract.tour_seo_pack) on a miss. That needs write grants and RLS decisions for tenant-path roles that today only read seo_context. The migration item only mentions read grants. Either the tenant paths build in memory and never write, or the grant model must be designed and reviewed.

Replay determinism. t2_seo was split out so the WM-20 release-0 replay rebuilds the same prompt. An upserted, overwritten pack changes the T2 prompt between a run and its replay. job.result records only pack_status and markets, not the content or a hash of it.

The new job kinds ignore the DM-11.4 gates. tour_seo_pack_build (debounced after every atomize, tour recompute and alias write), the nightly sweep and seo_coverage_watch are all queued/running rows inside BUSY_HORIZON_S. During a wave or after a big research run they block DB Migrate apply (IDLE_EXEMPT_KINDS['shared'] is empty, run_migration.py:213) and possibly Deploy Dev. The design never says which kinds are deploy_gate_exempt or deploy_blocking, or that the Infra exempt list must be updated alongside them.

The alert channel does not fit. 'Opens or updates one issue using the root CI-hygiene pattern' is a GitHub/CI pattern. A CIS worker job in a public repo has no token for that. The house pattern for $0 watchdogs is shared/ops_checks.alert_all (admin bell + one SNS e-mail per day), as quality_funnel_watch_job does. A daily job is also excessive for data that only changes after an approved run or an atomize: attach it to the existing daily report chain or the data-coverage page.

The run shape is fragile. Phase 1 as one segment_research job means about 5.4k SERP calls at SERP_CONCURRENCY=4 with no rate pacing. That is plausibly 1.5-2.5 h against expected_seconds=3600 and max_attempts=2. segment_research_log is written only in phase E at the end, so a deploy SIGTERM or crash leaves every place due. The retry re-runs proposal and SERP selection, and SERPs bought before the crash are only skipped if the new PAA cache check lands first. One malformed keyword fails a whole 1,000-keyword task and marks ~390 places failed. The design names keyword sanitising but not resumability or chunking.

Refreshes expire all at once. The whole catalogue is bought in one week, so every volume row ages past 182 days together (~May 2027) and every PAA row at 365 days. The result is a 10-11 USD lump that needs a top-up and an approval on a deadline. Readers do not filter by freshness, so there is no data cliff. But the guard will page at 100% stale on one day, and the plan hinges on remembering the lump. A rolling oldest-first refresh inside the monthly cap costs the same in task terms with 1,000-keyword chunks.

A 182-day volume refresh is unjustified for a startup. Google Ads volumes are 12-month averages, and the Blog bar is a ≥1000 threshold. Refreshing volumes every 365 days halves a recurring cost for no product loss. The design keeps 182 days without arguing for it.

Scope creep for a 1-2 person team. About 22 code items cover a migration with a PK change on segment_research_log, 2 tables, 4 columns, a view, 2 new job kinds plus a sweep, 5 rebuild triggers, read-through writes, a T9 keyword-selection change, Slate semantics, A3 English filtering and a Debate contested writer. The contested writer and the T9 keyword rework are not needed to make DFS spend optimal or to feed T2/S1. They change product behaviour and should be separate issues.

S1 behaviour regresses until research covers a tour. The S1_SEO_BUY default is false, so any S1 wave run before Phase 1 completes, or on tours whose places are not yet researched, gets keyword-less output. The only safeguard is a runbook step ('scoped research before the wave'), and runbook steps get skipped. This needs a hard guard: the wave refuses to start, or warns in /admin/waves, when its pack coverage is below a threshold.

Freshness is ambiguous in v_research_due. It says 'no fresh volume row for a target market', but the log becomes per tier. If due is computed from search_demand while the log is written per place, a place whose purchase partly failed, or that was renamed, can be bought again or skipped inconsistently. One source of truth for 'due' is needed, and the design does not pick one.

Renames are not handled. place_keyword_map is keyed on canonical_place text. A re-atomize wave that renames places (how many of the 7,116 stale places are renames is unmeasured) orphans map rows, pays the LLM again, and inflates the '300 places/month' assumption with no measurement.

There is no plan for the off-ledger drain. The balance pre-check and monthly cap assume the ledger equals the bill, but 0.7-1.5 USD left the account on 27/10, 28/10 and 01/11 with no ledger rows. A plausible suspect is another tool sharing the DFS credentials, for example a claude.ai DataforSEO connector on the same account; unverified. Without a reconcile step a monthly cap of 5 USD is not an honest ceiling.

Tenant-owned tours are unclear. The place-country SQL filters owner_scope='platform'. The design does not say whether tenant-scope tours or atoms enter v_research_due or the packs, or how packs for them stay isolated per tenant.
strengths: Buying a single SERP per place at US/en instead of one per market is the right cost lever. It removes about 5 x 11 USD of SERP versus today's shape, and the reason holds: every PAA consumer keeps English only.

There is exactly one DFS buyer, S1 becomes read-only, and an import-guard test bans DFS from tenant, T2, Slate, T8, T9 and pack modules. This closes the whole class of failure behind the 49 USD incident on 25/09 and the October S1 spend.

Research enqueues a debounced platform recompute through the existing coalescing (recompute_job.py:70-116). This fixes the verified gap (4 to 31 Blog-eligible only after a manual recompute) with code that already exists.
The T2 keyword_fit filter ships before the purchase, which shows awareness of the DFS_INTENT_UNDERUSED −1.0 penalty under the S271 validate-only status. A ~3-tour before/after trial is planned.

Approval is per phase, there is a USD gate instead of MAX_PLACES_PER_RUN, estimate_cost is recalibrated, and the first 1,000-keyword task is checked against dfs_call_log with an abort above 0.09. That is a sensible guard for the one price that has never been observed.
Persisting place_keyword_map means a second market or a refresh does not pay the LLM again, and it enables exact keyword joins instead of ILIKE.

Slate takes the MAX across the tenant's markets and splits no-data from below-bar. This fixes the best-rank CTE bug where a thin DE/FR/NL market hides real US/UK demand, and it meets the 'done when' of AA-1055.
The proxy market map with UI labels replaces silently dropped markets. The cost is free and it is honest to staff and tenants.
Readers do not filter by retrieved_on, so a late refresh degrades gently instead of falling off a cliff. The design correctly gives packs no TTL of their own.
steal: Make the writer unit a pure shared loader with no table (approach A): `seo_pack(conn, tour_id, markets) -> dict` used by S1, T2, T8, T9 and quarter-plan. Store the loaded pack (or its content hash plus keyword list) in each job's result for audit and replay. Add a materialised table later only if loader latency is measured as a problem. This drops the sweep, the 5 triggers, the read-through writes and the tenant write grants.

Split Phase 1 into one job per country (about 14) under a single approval with an aggregate USD cap. Write segment_research_log per place as each place completes, not in phase E. Add rate pacing, keyword sanitising, and split-and-retry of a failed 1,000-keyword task (halve it) so one bad keyword cannot fail ~390 places. Keep each job under expected_seconds.

Refresh on a rolling basis: each monthly run takes the oldest-first slice of due places up to the monthly cap (1/12 of the catalogue a month). No May-2027 lump, no deadline top-up, no 100%-stale alert spike. Volume freshness at 365 days instead of 182.

Reconcile the DFS balance: record the balance before and after every paid run (fetch_balance is free) and compare the delta with the dfs_call_log sum. Alert on drift above 0.10 USD, modelled on llm_cost_reconcile_job. Check whether any connector or tool outside CIS shares the DFS credentials.

Use ops_checks.alert_all (bell + SNS) and the existing daily report chain for coverage alerts, not a new daily job opening GitHub issues. Register any new kind as deploy_gate_exempt or deploy_blocking explicitly, and mirror the decision in infra run_migration.py IDLE_EXEMPT_KINDS in the same PR wave.

Wave pre-flight hard guard: /admin/waves refuses to start, or warns, when its tours' places have no fresh volume, and offers a one-click scoped research run with a cost preview. Do not rely on the runbook step.

Make segment_research_log the single source of truth for 'due', per (place, market, tier). Treat search_demand only as the value store. Key place_keyword_map on canonical place id (or keep an alias table) so renames reuse proposals.

Minimal Phase 0 scope for a small team: scope filter (transit, unnamed, orphan), SERP once at US/en with a PAA cache skip, persisted keyword map, research-to-recompute link, T2 keyword_fit, Slate MAX + no-data split, tenant DFS import guard, ledger tenant_id/job_id. Defer the contested writer, the T9 keyword rework and the A3 English-only question filter to separate issues with their own before/after measurement.

Put the first post-Phase-1 platform recompute behind a budget for Jev decide() calls and Cohere embeddings, with a dry-run count of candidate (segment, keyword) pairs before it runs, and keep it out of wave windows.
